title: UI priority: what shows where (less busy, less text)
body:
> Part of #2 · Applies to #4 (S1, conversations) and #9 (S4, HUD/Menu/Map). Both must follow this spec.

The owner on 2026-10-10:

> "tbh my problem rn is the UI is too busy. and it's all very text heavy and not intuitive. Not that everything is "hidden" tbh I think the priority on what to show vs hide (somewhere that can later still be accessed) is shit."

So the fix is **priority**: each moment shows the one or two things that matter, and everything else sits one tap away in the menu. This replaces decision 4 on #2 ("hide the numbers behind Scholar's View").

## Rules

1. **One job per moment.** Walking shows where people are. Talking shows what they said and what you can say. Anything else waits in the menu.
2. **Visuals over sentences.**
   - Thresholds become marks on a bar ("Backing at 80 · Allegiance at 100" becomes two notches).
   - Status becomes an icon state (bond beads, the suspicion eye).
   - No rule paragraphs anywhere except the menu's Rules page.
3. **Short words.** HUD and toast text stays under about 8 words. Names and quoted dialogue are the only exception.
4. **Everything stays reachable.** Exact numbers, rules, factions, plots and saves all live in the menu.
5. **The menu works with touch.** It opens from an always-visible seal button (Esc also opens it on desktop). No hold-to-peek keys, no hover-only info.

## What shows where

| Moment | On screen | Gone from today's screen |
|---|---|---|
| **Walking** (always on) | Minimap with people dots, tinted by bond, with a cinnabar edge if hostile. The season time is the minimap's ring, burning down like incense. A small purse (ingot plus number) beside it. The menu seal. | Brand plaque, the 3-number stat bar, the Notifications/Profile/Court/Next season buttons, the 2D toggle, the zone title, the separate clock and countdown, the controls strip, the hint line, the Save & game button |
| **Near something** | One prompt row ("Speak with Consort Rong"). The courtier's floating name gets one bond icon, plus a warning mark if they're dangerous. | The "Approach a courtier or a marked palace gate" hint |
| **Conversation** | Their line. Your 2-4 choices. A nameplate with bond beads and the suspicion eye. Witness marks when someone can see you. | The stat dossier, the Support/Affection bars, the threshold sentences, the "About" drawer, the "Effects & other actions" and "Romance" drawers |
| **Something happens** | One-line toast, at most 2 on screen, gone in about 3 s. Big moments (promotion, plot, the Emperor) get a ceremony. | Browser `alert()`s, pinned banners |
| **Goal changes** | The new goal slides in under the minimap for a few seconds, then lives in the menu. | Goal text only existing in 2D |
| **First run only** | A controls hint that fades after about 20 s. | The permanent controls strip |

The purse always shows, but small. It pops (`PopNumber`) when it changes and gets bigger at the steward's stall.

## The menu (one tap or Esc)

- **Goals:** promotion progress with exact standing and influence numbers, deadline, schemes against you.
- **People:** everyone you've met, with exact support, affection, suspicion and hate, plus Brush Notes.
- **Satchel, Map, Factions.**
- **Rules:** every mechanic paragraph that exists today, moved here.
- **Settings and Save.**

Exact numbers live **only** here. The Scholar's View toggle from the plan is dropped. Numbers are always one tap away, so no in-world numbers mode is needed.

## Touch and tablet

- Same layers. The minimap is about 112 px on phones, and the menu seal sits in a thumb-reachable corner.
- Conversation choices become a bottom sheet with large rows.
- Nothing depends on hover, a held key or a keyboard shortcut.

## Done when

- While walking, the persistent HUD is exactly: the minimap (with the time ring and people), the purse and the menu seal. The interaction prompt and toasts appear only when needed.
- A conversation screen has no paragraph text and no bars.
- Every number and rule that exists today can be found in the menu.
- Checked on desktop and on a tablet-sized window (devtools is fine).
- Owner playtests and says it's calm.

title: Early game feels empty: few reachable courtiers and the hall fills from the far end
body:
## What happens
- A new Concubine can only enter the Ladies' Court. On average about 3.8 of the ~14 active courtiers are there at a time.
- At the starting rank a Concubine can never meet 19 of the 48 courtiers, and a Scholar can never meet 20 of 48. The first promotion (Consort or Minister) opens the rest.
- Only 2 of the 4 majors (Crown Prince, Prime Minister, Empress Consort, Empress Dowager) are in the active cast each season until the first promotion. After that it's 3.
- In the 3D palace the player spawns at the south end of the hall. Courtiers are placed from the north end, about 37 m away in the Ladies' Court. Walking is the default speed, so reaching the first courtier takes about 27 s unless you hold Shift.

Nothing here is broken. The early game is thin by design and needs fixing.

## Where
- Rank access: `src/lib/careerAccess.ts:28` `concubine:['common','ladies']`, `src/lib/careerAccess.ts:25` `scholar:['common','emperor','library']`. Consort (`:29`) and Minister (`:26`) open the other rooms.
- Schedules that never enter those rooms: `src/palace/zones.ts:45-48`, `:60-68` (Prime Minister, Scholars, Generals, Ministers, Princes never visit the Ladies' Court). Concubines, consorts, maids and the two Empresses never visit the Library or the Emperor's palace.
- Active cast: `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:68` `const desiredMajorCount = playerRank ? 3 : 2;`. `rank` is `null` until the first promotion (`game-machine.ts:143`, set at `:1249`). Cast size is 12-16 from `activeCastMin/Max` (`src/lib/campaignBalance.ts:14-15`, used at `game-machine.ts:94`).
- Placement: `src/palace/world.ts:293` builds candidates from `bounds.minZ+6` upward. The minimap marks minZ as north (`src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:465`). Spawn is `maxZ-5` (`src/palace/zones.ts:25`). Courtiers with no saved pose take the first valid candidate (`world.ts:300`). Patrol stops come from the early candidate indices (`world.ts:306`), so roaming courtiers stay in the north half. Majors other than the Dowager don't roam (`world.ts:308`).
- Speed: `src/palace/characterModels.ts:79` sets walk 1.35 and run 3.8. `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:323` only runs while Shift or the touch sprint toggle is held.

Simulated over 400 seeds with `campaignRandom` and the same pool logic, season 1, all 4 phases:

| Career | Rooms open | Avg courtiers present in those rooms | Phases with nobody |
|---|---|---|---|
| Concubine | Ladies' Court | 3.8 | 3 / 1600 |
| Scholar | Library, Emperor's palace | 6.3 | 0 |
| Prince | Empress's, Dowager's, Library | 9.7 | 0 |

## How to reproduce
1. `npm run dev`, open http://localhost:5173 and pick Concubine.
2. Don't touch Shift. The hall ahead looks empty, and the courtiers are near the far (north) wall.
3. Walk to the nearest courtier and time it (roughly 25-30 s).
4. Open the court roster. Ministers, Scholars, Generals, Princes and the Prime Minister show up in the seasonal pool, but you can never find them in the Ladies' Court.

To check the counts without the game: loop `scheduledNpcZone(name, season, progress)` over all 48 names and test the result against `RANK_ACCESS[rank]`.

## Suggested fix
Minute-one fixes (already planned in Slice 1):
- Sort placement candidates by distance to the player's entry point. That's spawn for a fresh entry and the gate when entering through a door. Use the entry point, not `zoneSpawn` alone.
- Keep patrol `destinations` spread across the room. The red team noted that sorting by spawn alone pulls every route south.
- Make run the default and relabel the touch toggle "Walk".
- Test through `createPalaceWorld`: the first NPC is within 15 m of the entry point and at least 2 are visible from it.

Cast and reachability (owner call):
- Guarantee a curated opening cast for the starting room. For example, at least 5-6 courtiers whose schedule includes the career's entry zone in season 1. Draw it from the seeded campaign RNG inside `selectCharacterPool`.
- Questions for the owner:
  - Should a starting Concubine stay locked to one room, or get a visiting slot (for example the Empress's palace in one watch)?
  - Should both Empresses be guaranteed for a Concubine start?
  - Should a few schedules visit across career lines, so locked-out courtiers can be met before promotion?
- Whatever is chosen, keep access in `careerAccess` and schedules in `zones.ts`. Don't add a second gating path.

## Related
- Slice 1: The Scene (placement near the entry point, run by default). Tracking: #2
- Slice 5: Watches and the living court (routines on authored spots replace candidate-grid placement)
- Red-team "Should fix": placement must use the entry point and keep routes spread out, and the opening cast is random 12-16 of 48 so the first-10-minutes script needs a guaranteed cast

title: Balance doc numbers are stale and the documented simulator command crashes on a missing folder
body:
## What happens
- `CAMPAIGN_BALANCE.md` gives gift and influence numbers that no longer match the game. An agent tuning balance from the doc will tune against the wrong numbers.
- The balance simulation command in `AGENTS.md` crashes with `ENOENT` once all runs finish. With the default arguments that is 30+ seconds of work, and none of it gets printed.

## Where

**Stale numbers in `CAMPAIGN_BALANCE.md`**. The source of truth is `CAMPAIGN_BALANCE` in `src/lib/campaignBalance.ts`.

| Topic | Doc says | Code says |
|---|---|---|
| Starting gifts | "Start50 gifts" (`CAMPAIGN_BALANCE.md:40`) | `startingGifts: 0` (`src/lib/campaignBalance.ts:17`). Picking a career grants the bottom-rank allowance right away (`src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:437`), so a run starts with 20 (Concubine, Scholar) or 25 (Prince) |
| Rank allowance | "each committed season adds50" (`:40`) | `seasonalGiftsByRank` gives 20 to 65 by rank (`src/lib/campaignBalance.ts:18`) |
| Influence gates | Prince 70/85%, Scholar 55/80%, Concubine 30/65% (`:30`) | `[0.70, 0.78]`, `[0.55, 0.72]`, `[0.30, 0.60]` (`src/lib/campaignBalance.ts:10-12`) |
| Promotion influence | "grants12 influence points" (`:30`) | `promotionInfluence: 0.03`, which is 3 points (`src/lib/campaignBalance.ts:22`) |
| Influence scaling of positive gifts | "up to25%" (`:30`) | `relativeInfluencePenalty: 0.50`, up to ±50% (`src/lib/campaignBalance.ts:27`, `:76`) |
| Tribute | "Tribute remains10" (`:40`). This also contradicts the doc's own `:69` | `tributeCosts: [10,20,40]` (`src/lib/campaignBalance.ts:19`) |

The doc's simulation results (`:59`) also predate this tuning. Line 74 admits it.

**Simulator default path**
- `scripts/simulate-campaign.ts:139`:
  ```ts
  writeFileSync(process.env.SIM_REPORT_PATH??`validation/campaign-simulation${...}.json`, ...);log(JSON.stringify(summaries,null,2));
  ```
- The repo has no `validation/` directory. `writeFileSync` throws before `log(...)` runs, so you get no summary either.
- The command is documented at `AGENTS.md:31`, `README.md:10` and `CAMPAIGN_BALANCE.md:50`.

## How to reproduce
1. Run `ROLE_FILTER=prince POLICY_FILTER=bad node --import tsx scripts/simulate-campaign.ts 1 1 2` from a clean checkout. This is a tiny run that finishes fast.
2. It fails with `ENOENT ... path: 'validation/campaign-simulation.json'` at `scripts/simulate-campaign.ts:139`.
3. For the doc: compare `CAMPAIGN_BALANCE.md:30` and `:40` with `src/lib/campaignBalance.ts:10-27`.

## Suggested fix
- **Simulator**:
  - Print the summaries before writing the report.
  - Create the report folder first (`mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true })`), or change the default to a path that always exists, such as `os.tmpdir()`.
  - Keep `SIM_REPORT_PATH` as the override.
  - Use one command form everywhere: `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` and the balance doc (which currently omits the `1 60` arguments).
- **Doc**:
  - Remove the duplicated numbers from `CAMPAIGN_BALANCE.md` and point to `CAMPAIGN_BALANCE` in `src/lib/campaignBalance.ts` as the single source (AGENTS.md rule 6: one concept, one place).
  - Keep only the design rationale: why the gates differ by career, why the Concubine route is slower, how recovery works.
  - Mark the old simulation results as historical, or replace them with a fresh run.
  - Use glossary words: **rank allowance**, **influence**, **global support**, **tribute**.
- Don't add a test that regex-matches the markdown against the source. AGENTS.md bans source-text tests.

## Related
- Slice 2: Real presents. It replaces the gift currency, so the gift section of this doc gets rewritten there anyway. Slice 2 also needs the simulator baseline recorded first. The plan works around the crash with `SIM_REPORT_PATH=/tmp/...`, but the simulator fix should land before or with that baseline so the documented command works for everyone.
- Tracking: #2

title: Remove dead UI branches: locked audience panel, unused toast, quest CSS, dead exports
body:
## What happens
- Several UI branches can never render, or tell the player something false. The next agent has to read through them and keep their tests passing anyway.
- The "They won't receive you yet / Requires N% influence" audience panel and the roster's "Influence required" label can never show. The audience gate always allows.
- "Evaluating message…" on the Send button suggests a slow judgement. The evaluation is a synchronous function, so the label flashes for about one render at most.
- `CharacterResponse` (a Tailwind white-box toast) is never imported.
- The `.palace-quest` quest banner CSS has no component.
- Ten exports listed in the architecture hygiene backlog have no callers.

## Where
**1. Audience gate always allows**
- `src/lib/influenceGating.ts:57-60`: `case 'interaction': ... return { allowed: true };`. Line 30 also discards the inputs: `void playerStats; void rank;`.
- `src/lib/influenceGating.ts:74-83`: the "refuses interaction entirely" branch is unreachable.
- `src/components/ActionButtons.tsx:45-52`: the locked panel. Its threshold formula `character.personalityVectors.influence - 0.3` is a leftover of a rule that no longer exists.
- `src/components/CourtRoster.tsx:28` and `:43-44`: `locked` is always false, so "Influence required" never shows.
- Always-true checks: `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:323` (`access.canInteract.allowed && ...`), `game-machine.ts:774`, and `src/components/GameLayout.tsx:310` (the season-start "approachable" search reduces to "first courtier with data").
- Dead styles: `.locked-audience` in `src/style.css:455-456` and `src/ui/theme/skin.css:39`.
- `tests/courtStrategy.test.ts:245-254` asserts `canInteract.allowed === true` for every case.

**2. "Evaluating message…" over a sync call**
- `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:293-297`: `evaluateGift: fromPromise(async ({ input }) => processGiftWithMessage(...))`.
- `src/lib/checkMessage.ts:42`: `processGiftWithMessage` is a plain synchronous function.
- `src/components/ActionButtons.tsx:78`: `{pending ? "Evaluating message…" : ...}`.
- `tests/giftTransactions.test.ts:302` asserts the label. `tests/giftTransactions.test.ts:306` replaces the `evaluateGift` actor through `provide()` to test the refund path. The refund behaviour is worth keeping; the async actor is just how it is tested today.

**3. Unused toast**
- `src/components/CharacterResponse.tsx`: nothing in `src/` or `tests/` imports it. It also uses `useEffect` and web-box classes (`bg-white rounded-lg shadow-lg`), which break the UI rules.

**4. Orphan quest CSS**
- `src/palace/palace.css:5`: `.palace-quest`, `.quest-diamond`, `.palace-quest strong` and `.palace-quest p`. No component renders these classes. (`.palace-warning` on the same line is live, see `GameLayout.tsx:400`.)

**5. Dead exports** (`docs/architecture/README.md:73`). Each one appears only on its own definition line:
- `handlePromotion`: `src/lib/influenceFear.ts:52`
- `calculateAmbitiousMessageEffects`: `src/lib/crossCharacterEffects.ts:15`
- `calculateFactionEffects`: `src/lib/factionSystem.ts:93`
- `consortHostility`: `src/lib/courtIntrigue.ts:11`
- `careerWindow`: `src/lib/campaignBalance.ts:80`
- `graphBackers`: `src/lib/courtGraph.ts:78`
- `getRank`: `src/lib/helpers.ts:3`
- `hasPromotedOffice`: `src/lib/influenceGating.ts:4`
- `getDisabledActions`: `src/lib/influenceGating.ts:98`
- `PALACE_CRAFT_LIGHTING`: `src/palace/palaceCraft.ts:266`

## How to reproduce
1. Read `checkActionAvailability` in `src/lib/influenceGating.ts`. The `interaction` case has no condition.
2. Run `grep -rnw "CharacterResponse" src tests`. Only the component's own file matches.
3. Run `grep -rn "palace-quest\|quest-diamond" src`. Only `src/palace/palace.css` matches.
4. For each name in the dead-export list, run `grep -rnw "<name>" src tests scripts`. Each returns one line, the definition.
5. In game: give any gift and watch the Send button. "Evaluating message…" is gone before you can read it.

## Suggested fix
Delete. Don't wrap or hide anything (AGENTS.md "Replace, don't layer").
- Remove the `interaction` action from `influenceGating`, along with `canInteract`, the unreachable all-blocked branch, the locked panel in `ActionButtons`, the roster's `locked`/"Influence required" branch, and the `canInteract` terms in `game-machine.ts:323`, `:774` and `GameLayout.tsx:310`. Delete the `.locked-audience` rules. Update `tests/courtStrategy.test.ts:245-254` to match.
- Delete `src/components/CharacterResponse.tsx`.
- Delete the `.palace-quest` and `.quest-diamond` rules from `src/palace/palace.css`. Removing frozen legacy CSS is allowed.
- Delete the ten dead exports, then remove that bullet from the hygiene backlog in `docs/architecture/README.md`.
- For "Evaluating message…": Slice 2 deletes `evaluateGift` and the `pendingGift` phases outright. If this cleanup lands first, the smallest honest change is to drop the pending label text and keep the button disabled while pending. Leave the actor alone, since the refund tests depend on it until Slice 2 replaces them with a synchronous gift transaction.
- Run `npm run check` and `npm run build`.

## Related
- Epic: #2
- Slice 1: The Scene deletes `ActionButtons.tsx`, which takes the locked panel and the label with it. The locked-panel cleanup can land now on its own, since it touches no machine or save code.
- Slice 2: Real presents deletes `evaluateGift`, the `pendingGift` phases and `influenceGating`.
- `CharacterResponse`, the `.palace-quest` CSS and the dead exports are not covered by any slice. They are pure hygiene and can go in any small PR.

title: 3D palace reloads the whole zone every quarter-season when the courtier roster shifts
body:
## What happens
- About every 2.5 minutes of play (default 10-minute season), the 3D zone tears itself down and builds again. The renderer is disposed, its WebGL context is forcibly lost, and a new one is created.
- The player sees the "Loading your character… Your season clock is paused." curtain until the player model is ready again. The season clock stops for that time.
- Courtiers who left the zone vanish. New arrivals appear out of nowhere at grid spots. Nobody walks in or out.
- All character art is decoded again on every rebuild, because decoded models are lease-counted and get released on dispose. Only the compressed bytes stay cached.

Not affected: an open conversation. The clock pauses while a conversation is open, so the roster can't change mid-conversation. Courtiers who stay in the zone keep their saved position and facing.

## Where
- `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:106-108`: the roster key depends on the season clock.
  ```ts
  const currentPeople=zoneRoster(people,zone,season,seasonProgress,playerType);
  const rosterKey=currentPeople.map(p=>p.name).join('|');
  ```
- `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:110-113`: the main scene effect creates the renderer and world, then calls `setReady(false)` and `onRenderReady(false)`.
- `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:446`: the cleanup calls `world.dispose()`, `renderer.dispose()`, `renderer.forceContextLoss()` and `canvas.remove()`.
- `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:448`: the deps are `[rosterKey,playerType,zone,visits]`.
- `src/palace/zones.ts:39-40`: `scheduledNpcZone` splits each season into four visit periods (`Math.floor(progress*4)`). Most offices move between periods (Emperor, eunuchs, maids, generals and so on), so in practice every zone's roster changes at every quarter. A quick `zoneRoster` run over a sample cast showed a change in all five zones at all three boundaries.
- `src/components/GameLayout.tsx:375`: `seasonProgress={1-secondsLeft/(seasonMinutes*60)}`.
- `src/persistence/campaignSave.ts:47`: the default `seasonMinutes` is 10.
- `src/components/GameLayout.tsx:233`: `!renderReady` is part of `clockPaused`, which is why the clock stops during the curtain.
- `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:477`: the loading curtain.
- `src/palace/world.ts:297-303`: a saved NPC pose is reused only when `saved.zone===zone` and the spot is still free. Everyone else gets the next candidate grid spot.

## How to reproduce
1. Start a campaign in 3D with the default 10-minute season.
2. Stand in any zone and don't open menus or conversations.
3. When the season clock crosses 7:30, 5:00 and 2:30 remaining, the loading curtain flashes and the courtier set changes in place.
4. Optional: watch WebGL context loss and recreation in the browser devtools console or performance panel at the same moments.

## Suggested fix
- Remove `rosterKey` from the main effect deps at `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:448`. Rebuild only on `zone`, `playerType` and `visits`.
- Add a roster sync step owned by the palace world (for example `syncRoster(arrivals, departures)`). It acquires model leases for arrivals and releases them for departures. The same live-ref pattern `updateSeason` already uses (`PalaceScene.tsx:449`) can drive it. Don't add a new `useEffect` without the owner's approval.
- Arrivals walk in from the gate of the zone they came from. Departures walk to their destination's gate and are then removed. A courtier the player is talking to delays leaving until the conversation closes.
- Send `onPresenceChange` when a courtier actually arrives or leaves. Today `PalaceScene.tsx:453-457` sends it after the rebuild.
- Replace, don't layer. Once roster sync lands, delete any transition used to mask the rebuild.
- Tests through the interface: after a sync plus N world steps, departures are gone, arrivals are in place, the scene object count is stable and leases are released. The Emperor entrance tests stay green.

## Related
- Slice 10: Walk in, walk out. That slice removes `rosterKey` from the deps and adds the director's `syncRoster`.
- Slice 5: Watches and the living court. Until Slice 10 lands, Slice 5 hides this rebuild behind the watch transition.
- Tracking: #2

title: Insult copy hides that spitting sets hate to 100 and makes a permanent enemy
body:
## What happens - The insult copy above "Spit in Face" lists support and suspicion only. It never says the courtier's **hate** jumps to 100. That turns them into an enemy for good, and once you hold rank 1 or higher they can start a **plot** against you. - The copy also skips the faction fallout. Every other member of the target's faction gains +0.1 **suspicion**. - About 100 ms after the insult, a browser `alert()` pops up ("Your insult has disturbed N faction members"). - "Spit in Face" is an ordinary button with no confirm step. It sits inside a collapsed "Effects & other actions" section, so the copy is easy to miss. ## Where - Copy and button: `src/components/ActionButtons.tsx:85-89` - `

Insult: lose up to 20 support, gain {... "50" : "30"} suspicion. Costs no gifts.

` - `` - Relationship reducer: `src/lib/courtGraph.ts:57` - `case 'spit':next.support=clamp(next.support-20);if(!immune)next.hate=100;break;` - `immune` comes from `hateIsBlocked` (`src/lib/courtGraph.ts:31`): a pledge or the same formal faction. - What hate 100 unlocks: - Enemy at hate >= 60: `src/lib/campaignBalance.ts:34`, `:75`. Positive gifts to an enemy are scaled to 10%: `src/lib/campaignBalance.ts:30`, `:78`. - Romance refused at hate >= 60: `src/lib/courtRomance.ts:3`, `:24`. - A plot against the player becomes possible at hate >= 80 once the player is rank 1 or higher: `src/lib/courtPlots.ts:31`. - Hate only resets when a pledge forms (`src/lib/courtGraph.ts:64`), and a pledge needs support 100. With gifts at 10%, that is close to unreachable. - Delayed side effect: `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:837-879` - A `setTimeout(..., 100)` reads actor snapshots, calls `calculateSpitInFaceEffects` (`src/lib/crossCharacterEffects.ts:81`), mutates other actors through `applyCrossCharacterEffects`, then calls `console.log` (`:872`) and `alert()` (`:873`). - The only other mention is the faction help panel: "Spitting adds full hate" (`src/components/GameLayout.tsx:488`). It is on a different screen and never says what full hate means. ## How to reproduce 1. Start a campaign as a Prince and get promoted to rank 1. 2. Talk to a courtier with influence <= 0.6 who is outside your formal faction and not pledged. 3. Open "Effects & other actions" and read the insult line. It says nothing about hate or plots. 4. Click "Spit in Face". If the target belongs to a faction other than Independent, a browser alert appears shortly after. 5. Open the stats or relationship view. The courtier's hate is 100 and they count as an enemy. Over the next seasons they can start a plot against you. Code-only path: `tests/hateRules.test.ts:40` already asserts that hate reaches 100 after `SPIT_IN_FACE`. ## Suggested fix - Build the insult preview from one rules function that returns every effect. For example, a `previewInsult(graph, from, to, supportLevel)` in the module that owns the relationship reducer, returning `{ supportLoss, suspicionGain, hateAfter, becomesEnemy, canPlot, factionWitnesses }`. The copy renders from that result, so text and engine can't drift apart. - Say it in plain words when `becomesEnemy` is true, for example "They will become your enemy and may plot against you." - Mark the action as dangerous (cinnabar `ui-btn-primary` styling is reserved for the main action, so use a seal or warning treatment) and ask for a second click to confirm. No `window.confirm`. - Delete the `setTimeout` in `SPIT_IN_FACE`. Compute the faction suspicion in the same synchronous `assign` from a pure function that takes the graph and returns the changes. Replace the `alert()` and `console.log` with a notice. Do this as a replacement and keep no second path. - Keep the numbers (support -20, hate 100 unless immune, suspicion +0.5/+0.3, faction +0.1). Changing the balance is the owner's call. - No new `useEffect`/`useMemo`/`useCallback` without the owner's approval. ## Related - Slice 1: The Scene. Deletes `ActionButtons.tsx` and brings in "A cutting remark" in `ConversationChoices`, with risk shown from `preview.dangerous`. The warning copy and confirm step belong there. - Slice 2: Real presents. Deletes the `SPIT_IN_FACE` `setTimeout` and all five `alert()` calls in favour of `src/lib/notices.ts`, and adds `SOCIAL_ACT` with `act: remark`. - Tracking: #2

title: Season recap omits ally income, and pledges and backings happen without an announcement
body: ## What happens - The season recap ("A NEW SEASON AT COURT") shows only `+N rank allowance · leftover gifts retained`. Gifts sent by pledged allies that same season are left out. Afterwards the Gifts counter rises by more than the recap said, and nothing explains the difference. - When a courtier reaches 100 support, they pledge and send their first gift right away, mid-season. Nothing on screen names the pledge or the gift. The only signs are the header numbers animating and a badge on the Notifications button. - Backing (60/70/80) and pledge (100) award global support with no message. The header Global support number chimes, but it looks like part of the gift the player just gave. - The player can find the income in the Notifications list ("+5 gifts, Season 3"), or in the courtier panel ("Sends N gifts each season"). Both are passive and easy to miss. ## Where - Recap text: `src/palace/SeasonTransition.tsx:36` ```tsx +{giftGrant} rank allowance · leftover gifts retained ``` - The recap is given only the rank grant: `src/components/GameLayout.tsx:382` passes `giftGrant={context.lastSeasonGiftGrant ?? seasonalGiftGrant(...)}`. - `lastSeasonGiftGrant` holds the rank allowance only: `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:948`. - Ally income is paid later, in season settlement. It goes into `giftsRemaining` and `giftNotifications`, and the recap never sees it: `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:1179-1189` (`allyIncome += amount`). - First (courtship) gift on reaching 100 support: guard `giveGifts` at `src/state-machines/character-machine.ts:52`, which sends `CHARACTER_GAVE_GIFTS` at `src/state-machines/character-machine.ts:98`. The machine pays it immediately at `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:591-602`, and defers it only while settlement is pending. - Backing and pledge handlers update `supportPoints`, `standingAwards` and influence. Neither pushes any notice: `CHARACTER_GAVE_SUPPORT` at `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:566`, `CHARACTER_GAVE_ALLEGIANCE` at `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:576-590`. - Existing passive traces: the Gifts `PopNumber` (`src/components/GameHeader.tsx:23`), the Notifications unread badge (`src/components/GameHeader.tsx:26`), the list in `src/components/CourtNotifications.tsx`, and the courtier panel line at `src/components/CharacterInfo.tsx:39`. ## How to reproduce 1. Start a new run. Give gifts to one low-influence courtier until their support reaches 100. 2. Watch the screen at the moment of the pledge. The Gifts and Global support numbers animate, and the Notifications badge shows 1. Nothing names the pledge or the gift. 3. Note the Gifts total. Press Next season. 4. The recap says `+N rank allowance` for the rank grant only. Close it. The Gifts total has gone up by N plus the ally's 1, 5 or 10. ## Suggested fix - **Recap.** Show a per-ally income breakdown in the recap, for example "+20 rank allowance", then "Maid Ling sends 1", then "Consort Rong sends 5". Settlement already records each payment through `recordGiftNotification(name, amount, season)`. Add a pure selector next to it in `src/lib/courtNotifications.ts` that returns that season's entries, and pass the result to `SeasonTransition` as a prop. This needs no new machine state. Settlement records entries under the new season number, so the selector can filter on `recapSeason`. - **Pledge and backing notices.** Have the `CHARACTER_GAVE_ALLEGIANCE` and `CHARACTER_GAVE_SUPPORT` handlers return a notice as data in the same `assign`, naming who, what changed, and the global support award. React then renders the notice. Rules code must not call `alert` or play sounds itself. - **Pledge moment.** A pledge is a momentous event under the UI rules, so show a `` with a gong for it. Put the courtship gift in the same notice ("X pledges to you and sends 5 gifts"), so the Gifts counter change has a cause on screen. - Replace the current record with the new one, keeping a single record of what happened. Use the plan's `notices` module if it has landed. Otherwise extend `giftNotifications` into it, but don't keep two parallel ledgers. - Ask the owner before adding any new `useEffect`, `useMemo` or `useCallback` to show these. Derive what to show from machine context during render. - Tests: render `SeasonTransition` with `renderToStaticMarkup` and check that ally lines appear. Add a machine test in which a pledge produces one notice and pays its award once. Leave the source-regex `giftNotifications.test.ts` passing until slice 2 replaces it. ## Related - Slice 2: Real presents. Its `notices` module replaces `giftNotifications` and CourtNotifications, and it turns ally income into named items ("Maid Ling sends you osmanthus cakes"). The pledge and backing notices fit there. - Slice 5: Watches and the living court. It owns `SeasonTransition`. The plan's end-of-season recap scroll should list ally income. - Tracking: #2

title: Dossier hint words and fear readout disagree with how messages are scored
body:
## What happens
- The "About" drawer in the courtier dossier shows personality words ("Ambitious", "Loyal", "Fearful") based on different thresholds than the ones that decide a message's response. A courtier can score a matching ambitious or cautious message with no hint word, or show "Loyal" and still give a neutral response to loyal words.
- "Fear of you" shows the courtier's fear of the player. The cautious message scores on their personality fear, which the dossier never shows.
- `personalityVectors.trust` is rolled, saved and validated. No rule reads it.
- Each expansion courtier has an authored `brief` in `src/data/courtExpansion.ts`. Players never see it, and some briefs promise a lean that the roll ignores. Eunuch Gao is "loyal to order" but comes out Rebel in about 41% of campaigns.
- The gift picker shows the exact support change before you send (`src/components/ActionButtons.tsx:42`, `:74`), and that softens the damage today. The hint words still read as noise that disagrees with the numbers.

## Where
Hint words, `src/lib/helpers.ts:52-55`:
```ts
if (personalityVector.ambition > 0.7) hints.push("Ambitious");
if (personalityVector.loyalty > 0.6) hints.push("Loyal");
if (personalityVector.fear > 0.7) hints.push("Fearful");
```
Scoring, `src/lib/checkMessage.ts:18-23`:
- ambitious match: `ambition>=.6 && loyalty<=.5` (`:18`)
- loyal match: `loyalty>=.7` (`:21`)
- cautious match: `personality.fear>=.5` (`:23`)

Faction is a third set: Rebel at `ambition >= 0.7 && loyalty <= 0.5` (`src/lib/factionSystem.ts:31`).

Dossier, `src/components/CharacterInfo.tsx:30-37`:
- `:30` prints the hint string.
- `:34` `["Fear of you", character.relationshipVectors.fearOfPlayer]`. Personality fear is missing from the list.
- Rendered for every audience, 2D and 3D, from `src/components/GameLayout.tsx:156`.

Trust:
- Written only at `src/data/characters.ts:12`, `:23`, `:34`, `:61`.
- Checked only as a bounded number at `src/persistence/campaignSave.ts:85` and `src/lib/giftMessages.ts:31`.

Briefs:
- `src/data/courtExpansion.ts:40` `"brief": "Formal keeper of ceremony; loyal to order"` (Eunuch Gao). Other eunuch briefs carry a lean too: "receptive to reform" (`:50`), "court loyalist" (`:95`), "quiet reformer" (`:103`).
- `src/data/characters.ts:131` maps `COURT_EXPANSION` to blueprints and drops `brief`.
- `src/data/characters.ts:87-89`: every eunuch flips `random()<.5` for the rebel profile, whatever the name says. Generals get per-name bias (`:92`), eunuchs don't.

## How to reproduce
1. Read the code path: a courtier with ambition .65 and loyalty .40 gets no "Ambitious" word (`helpers.ts:52`), but an ambitious message scores a match (`checkMessage.ts:18`).
2. A courtier with loyalty .65 shows "Loyal" (`helpers.ts:54`), but a loyal message scores neutral (`checkMessage.ts:21` needs .7).
3. A courtier with personality fear .6 and fear of the player 0 shows "Fear of you 0%" and no "Fearful", but a cautious message scores a match (`checkMessage.ts:23`).
4. In game: open the dossier for several courtiers. Pick each message and compare the preview line with the hint words.
5. Gao: call `createInitialCharacters(Math.random)` 2000 times and run `assignCharacterFaction` on Eunuch Gao. I got Rebel 824, Loyalist 943, Independent 233.

## Suggested fix
- Give trait thresholds one owner. A small rules module (for example `courtierTraits`) takes `CharacterPersonalityVectors` and returns the readable traits ("ambitious", "devoted", "fearful"). `analyzeMessageChoice`, the dossier hint and the Slice 2 political taste tags all read from it. Then delete `getPersonalityHint`. Keep factions in `factionSystem`, and decide on purpose whether they share these thresholds.
- Pick one fear for the dossier. Either show personality fear next to "Fear of you" with labels that tell them apart, or let the hint carry it. Don't show only the vector the scoring ignores.
- Trust: either give it a real rule or delete it from the type, the generators, the gift-result check and the save validator. Removing it needs a save migration step in `src/persistence/`. Don't keep a field that nothing reads.
- Briefs: split each into an appearance note (art direction, fine to keep hidden) and a temperament line. Either bias the roll by name the way generals are biased (`characters.ts:92`, seeded `random`), or rewrite the lines so they don't promise a faction. If a brief is shown, it must agree with the rolled traits.
- Tests: call the traits module with boundary vectors and check that the dossier render (`renderToStaticMarkup`) and `analyzeMessageChoice` agree. Don't regex-match source.

## Related
- Slice 1: The Scene deletes the stat dossier and the "+19" preview. After that, hint text is the main way a player reads a courtier, so the thresholds have to match first.
- Slice 2: Real presents builds Brush Notes and the political taste tags from rolled traits at the `checkMessage.ts` thresholds. The single traits module belongs there.
- Tracking: ##2

title: Emperor audience verdict screen never shows; judging reads "Preparing Audience" and survivor path is dead
body:
## What happens
- After the third answer the audience screen says "Preparing Audience… The Emperor is considering his questions..." while the outcome is being judged. That can last up to 30 seconds. It reads as if the audience is starting over.
- The "The Emperor's Judgment" verdict scroll never shows. The game jumps straight to the ending screen (victory or execution) or back to the court with a demotion dialog (failure).
- On failure the Emperor's message is thrown away. The demotion dialog only shows fixed text.
- The `survivor` victory path, the "Refuse (Risk Execution)" warning and the fatal-refusal branch can never run. They are still typed, saved, rendered and given fallback questions.

## Where
**Verdict screen can't be reached**
- `src/state-machines/emperor-audience-machine.ts:143-158`: the final state `audience_complete` runs `sendParent({ type: 'EMPEROR_AUDIENCE_COMPLETE', ... })` on entry and also returns `output`.
- `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:1345` (`on.EMPEROR_AUDIENCE_COMPLETE`) and `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:1297` (`invoke.onDone`) are copies of the same two branches. Both leave `emperor_audience` at once, for `game_over` or `playing`.
- `src/components/GameLayout.tsx:369` renders `EmperorAudienceHandler` only while `machineState.matches("emperor_audience")`, so the screen unmounts on the same event that sets `outcome`.
- `src/components/GameLayout.tsx:70` (`isComplete = !!outcome`) and `src/components/EmperorAudienceScreen.tsx:94-107` (the verdict block and its `window.location.reload()` "Play Again" button) are dead.
- Victory and execution still show the Emperor's words through `src/components/GameOverScreen.tsx:94`. On failure, `emperorMessage` is stored at `game-machine.ts:1387` and never rendered. The audience demotion dialog shows `careerNotice` and `DemotionSummary` (`src/lib/demotionNotice.ts:7`).

**Judging shows the loading text**
- `src/state-machines/emperor-audience-machine.ts:91`: each answer increments `currentQuestionIndex`. After 3 answers it is `3`, and `always` moves to `judging_outcome` (`:95-99`, with a 30s timeout at `:133`).
- `src/components/EmperorAudienceScreen.tsx:46`: `questions[3]` is `undefined`. `outcome` is still `null`, so `:109-112` renders "Preparing Audience…".

**Survivor and max-suspicion refusal are dead**
- `src/lib/emperorAudience.ts:49-70`: `determineVictoryPath` returns only `traditional`, `shadow-ruler`, `revolutionary` or `null`.
- `survivor` still appears in `src/types/emperorAudience.ts:4` and `:59`, `src/lib/emperorAudience.ts:114` and `:171`, `src/lib/aiServices.ts:122`, `:215`, `:469` and `:521-556`, `src/data/fallbackQuestions.ts:113`, `src/components/EmperorAudienceOffer.tsx:25` and `:40`, `src/components/EmperorAudienceScreen.tsx:38`, and `src/persistence/campaignSave.ts:95` and `:147`.
- `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:604-629`: once **reports** reach the threshold, `CHARACTER_IS_SUSPICIOUS` goes straight to `game_over`. That means `isAtMaxSuspicion` is never true while the audience offer is open. The fatal `REFUSE_AUDIENCE` guard (`game-machine.ts:1271`) and the warning in `EmperorAudienceOffer.tsx:47` (`isAtMaxSuspicion && victoryPath === 'survivor'`) can't run.

## How to reproduce
1. Reach top rank, finish **consolidation** and join a faction. (Or run `node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern="audience" tests/gameMachine.test.ts` to follow the same path in code.)
2. Enter the **audience** and answer all three questions.
3. While the outcome is judged, the screen says "Preparing Audience…".
4. When the outcome arrives, the game skips the verdict scroll. On a failure, the Emperor's reply never appears.
5. To check the dead survivor code, read `determineVictoryPath`. No branch returns `'survivor'`.

## Suggested fix
- Give the audience machine one way to report its result. Keep `output` with `onDone` and delete the `sendParent` entry action and the duplicated `on.EMPEROR_AUDIENCE_COMPLETE` branches in `game-machine.ts`. That is a single place to change.
- Choose where the verdict lives, and delete the other place:
  - Either add a `verdict` substate to the parent. It holds the outcome until a new `ACKNOWLEDGE_VERDICT` event, then goes to `game_over` or applies the demotion.
  - Or delete the verdict block in `EmperorAudienceScreen` and show the Emperor's message on the failure path as well, in the demotion dialog.
- Render the judging phase explicitly. Pass the audience machine's state (`judging_outcome`) to the screen and show a "The Emperor weighs your answers" line. Don't rely on `questions[index]` being undefined.
- Delete `survivor` from `VictoryPath`, `GameContextData`, the AI prompts, the fallback questions, the offer copy and the background map. Delete the `isAtMaxSuspicion` refusal guard and the offer warning too. Bump the save validation in `campaignSave.ts` to match, with a migration that maps any stored `'survivor'` to `null`.
- Test through the interfaces. Drive the machine to a failure and assert that the message is still available after the transition. Render `EmperorAudienceScreen` in the judging state and assert it doesn't say "Preparing".
- No new `useEffect`, `useMemo` or `useCallback` is needed for any of this.

## Related
- Slice 8: The Night of Slips and the Emperor's scenes. It rewrites `EmperorAudienceScreen` and `GameOverScreen` and replaces the audience questions. Fix the state flow there, or before it as a small standalone PR.
- Owner decision on suspicion (section 11, option B, "Whispers against you") decides whether a max-suspicion refusal should exist at all.
- Tracking: #2

title: Gift replies use unseeded Math.random, are picked twice per gift, and share 18 lines
body:
## What happens

- After a gift, the courtier's reply is picked at random with `Math.random`. The pick doesn't use the seeded campaign RNG, so the same seed and the same moves can give different lines. Tests can't assert the line either.
- Every courtier draws from the same 18 lines (6 response types x 3 lines). All 48 people at court sound the same. Only the name prefix changes.
- Each gift picks a reply twice, in two places, and stores both. The two stored strings disagree about 2 times in 3. The player only ever sees the courtier actor's copy. The campaign-level copy is saved but never shown, so it is dead state.
- One more handler (`CHARACTER_RESPONDED`) also picks a reply, but nothing sends that event.

## Where

- `src/lib/getResponse.ts:2-37`: `getResponseByType(characterName, responseType)` holds the 18 lines and ends with
  `return responseList[Math.floor(Math.random() * responseList.length)];` (`:37`).
- Pick 1, shown to the player: `src/state-machines/character-machine.ts:82` sets the courtier actor's `lastResponse` from `getResponseByType(context.name, origin.result.responseType)`. Then `:86` sends `GIFT_APPLIED` to the campaign machine.
- Pick 2, stored but not shown: `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:513` handles `GIFT_APPLIED` with `lastCharacterResponse: getResponseByType(gift.characterId, event.response)`, a fresh, independent draw.
- Dead pick: `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:644-647` handles `CHARACTER_RESPONDED`, declared at `:279`. Nothing in `src/` sends this event.
- What the player sees:
  - `src/components/GameLayout.tsx:157`: the speech bubble uses `data.lastResponse` (the actor's pick). It falls back to the `response` prop (`lastCharacterResponse`, passed at `:427` and `:446`) only when the actor's line is empty.
  - `src/components/GameLayout.tsx:376`: the 3D `conversationReply` reads the actor's `lastResponse` only.
- Both copies are persisted: `src/persistence/campaignSave.ts:83` (courtier `lastResponse`) and `:144` (`lastCharacterResponse`).
- Latent hazard: `src/data/characters.ts:5` and `:134` default `random` to `Math.random`, and `:142` builds `initialCharacters` with it at import time. Today its consumers only read names and types, so vectors from that roster never reach gameplay. The campaign roster itself is seeded (`game-machine.ts:452`).

## How to reproduce

Read the code path, since the duplicate is invisible in-game:

1. Start a campaign, give a gift to any courtier and note the reply in the speech bubble.
2. Export or inspect the save. Compare the courtier's `lastResponse` with the campaign context's `lastCharacterResponse`. They are often different lines of the same response type.
3. Start a fresh game with the same seed and make the same gift. The reply line can change, while every other outcome is the same.
4. Give gifts to two different courtiers who roll the same response type. They draw from the same three lines.

## Suggested fix

- Pick the reply once per gift event, in one place. The courtier actor's `lastResponse` is the copy players see and saves keep, so keep that one.
- Drop `lastCharacterResponse` from the gift path (`game-machine.ts:513`). Feed the speech bubble only from the actor's `lastResponse`. Migrate saves that still carry `lastCharacterResponse`.
- Delete the dead `CHARACTER_RESPONDED` event type and handler (`game-machine.ts:279`, `:644-647`).
- Make the pick deterministic without spending `rngState`. A cosmetic draw keyed on a stable input (for example campaign seed, courtier name and gift `requestId`) keeps balance draws unchanged. The pick takes its inputs as arguments and returns a string ("accept dependencies, return results").
- Replace `getResponse.ts` with the planned voice module, then delete it ("replace, don't layer"). Don't add a seeded wrapper around the old 18-line table.
- In `src/data/characters.ts`, remove the `Math.random` defaults so callers must pass the campaign RNG. For the name and type tables that `initialCharacters` serves today, export a static blueprint list with no vectors.
- Tests through the interface:
  - The same inputs give the same line.
  - `rngState` is unchanged after a gift reply.
  - `Math.random` mocked to throw doesn't break a gift.
  - The line shown equals the stored `lastResponse`.

## Related

- Slice 3: Voices of the Ladies' Court. It replaces `getResponseByType` with `courtVoice`, draws once per event and deletes `getResponse.ts`. Note that the slice text says "3 call sites", but only two are live. The third is the dead `CHARACTER_RESPONDED` handler, which should simply be deleted.
- Tracking issue: ##2

title: 3D talk hides the gift and romance receipt along with the reply bubble
body:
## What happens
- In the 3D palace, when a courtier's reply is projected above her head, the in-dialog reply bubble is shrunk to a 1px screen-reader copy.
- The gift receipt lives inside that bubble, so it gets hidden with it. That's the line "Last political gift: +N personal support · N gifts (· +N global support)".
- The romance receipt sits in the same slot, so it's hidden too: "Romantic gift: +N affection · N gifts", "Romance accepted", "Proposal refused", "Romance ended".
- The support number in the dossier changes with no `PopNumber`. So a sighted 3D player sees the gift count drop and the courtier play a reaction, but never learns how much support the gift bought.
- The receipt only shows up when head projection fails (courtier off screen, more than 13 m away, behind a wall, software renderer, or no free spot for the bubble).

## Where
- `src/components/GameLayout.tsx:157-158`: `CourtAudience` renders both receipts as a `<small>` child of `CourtSpeechBubble`, with `anchored={speechAnchored}`.
- `src/components/CourtSpeechBubble.tsx:3`: `className={`court-speech ${anchored?'speech-accessible-copy':''}`}`. The children render inside the same `<section>`.
- `src/style.css:750`: `.speech-accessible-copy{position:absolute!important;width:1px!important;height:1px!important;...;overflow:hidden!important;clip-path:inset(50%)}`. These are `!important` rules in `@layer legacy`, so they beat the theme's `.court-speech` rules at `src/ui/theme/skin.css:539-553`.
- `src/components/GameLayout.tsx:181`, `:376`, `:442`: `speechAnchored` is set by `PalaceScene`'s `onSpeechProjectionChange` and passed to the 3D "A moment at court" dialog.
- `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:397-399`: the projected `.palace-head-speech` div only gets `${displayName}: ${reply}` as `textContent`. No receipt.
- `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:395-415`, `:435`: projection is on only when the courtier is visible, close, unobstructed, not on the software renderer, and `placeSpeech` finds a spot.
- `src/components/CharacterInfo.tsx:19`: support renders as a plain `{Math.round(character.supportLevel*10)/10}` with no `PopNumber`.
- For contrast, `src/components/GameHeader.tsx:22-23` does use `PopNumber` for global support and gifts.

## How to reproduce
1. `npm run dev`, open http://localhost:5173 and start any career.
2. In the 3D palace, walk up to a courtier who's in view and press E.
3. Send a political gift. The reply shows above her head.
4. Look at the dialog: no "Last political gift" line, and the dossier support number changes with no pop.
5. Optional: walk until she's off screen, or use a software-rendered browser, and talk again. The bubble and receipt now show in the dialog.

Read-the-code path: `GameLayout.tsx:442` → `CourtAudience` → `CourtSpeechBubble anchored` → `style.css:750`.

## Suggested fix
Short term, if the 3D talk dialog stays around for a while:
- Move both receipts out of `CourtSpeechBubble`'s children into their own visible line in `CourtAudience`, next to the choices, so the accessible-copy clip can't hide them.
- Show the support change in the dossier with `<PopNumber value={character.supportLevel} />` (and `cueOnGain` if that fits).
- Replace the `romanceUI` source-regex assertions that cover this area with a render test. Render `CourtAudience` with `speechAnchored` true and a receipt, then check that the receipt text is outside the `speech-accessible-copy` element.

Long term, Slice 1 removes this code path completely. Make sure the replacement doesn't lose the feedback:
- A receipt should always produce a visible reaction (petals or a leaf, a cue, and a worded toast) through `reactionFor(receipt)`. That covers romance receipts too.
- Whether exact support deltas show by default is an owner call. The plan hides them outside Scholar's View. Either way the player needs to see the gift's result in words.

## Related
- Slice 1: The Scene deletes the 3D "A moment at court" dialog, the speech div, `placeSpeech`/`speechPlacement.ts` and `onSpeechProjectionChange`, and adds `reactionFor` for gift and romance receipts. Part of #2.
- Slice 2: Real presents (toasts that say what you learned) covers the same feedback for item gifts.

title: Delete the Gemini audience path (key would ship in the bundle) and fix guessable answers
body:
## What happens
- If anyone builds with `VITE_GEMINI_API_KEY` set, the key gets inlined into the client JS and shows up in every audience request URL. Any player can read it from the bundle or the network tab. No key is committed today (`.env` is gitignored), so the leak is latent. It only takes one build with the variable set.
- The offline fallback already covers every failure, so the Gemini path adds nothing a player needs.
- The fallback audience can be gamed. Each path always gets the same three questions, in the same a/b/c order, with fixed right answers:
  - Survivor: a, a, a
  - Shadow-ruler: b, b, b
  - Traditional: a, b, b
  - Revolutionary: a, b, a
- Three right answers always clear the victory line, whatever the player's influence or loyalty. Once a player knows the pattern, the faction audience is a guaranteed win.

## Where
- `src/lib/aiServices.ts:314`: `const apiKey = import.meta.env.VITE_GEMINI_API_KEY;`
- `src/lib/aiServices.ts:324`: ``fetch(`https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/${AI_CONFIG.model}:generateContent?key=${apiKey}`, …)``
- `src/lib/aiServices.ts:371-433`: `generateQuestions` and `judgeOutcome` already fall back to `FALLBACK_QUESTIONS` and `getFallbackOutcome` on any error.
- `src/state-machines/emperor-audience-machine.ts:69-84`: the machine has a second fallback (`onError` and a 30s `after` timeout) that calls `getFallbackQuestions`.
- `src/lib/aiServices.ts:449,458`: `score = correctAnswers / questions.length`, and victory at `finalScore >= 0.75`. 3/3 gives 1.0, so the context bonus (capped at 0.3, `:530`) never matters for a player who knows the answers.
- `src/data/fallbackQuestions.ts`: `correctAnswer` sits at lines 17, 28, 39 (traditional), 52, 63, 74 (shadow-ruler), 87, 98, 109 (revolutionary) and 122, 133, 144 (survivor).
- `src/components/EmperorAudienceScreen.tsx:86`: options render through `Object.entries(currentQuestion.options)`, so the order is always a, b, c.
- Duplication: `getFallbackQuestions` exists in both `src/lib/aiServices.ts:566` and `src/data/fallbackQuestions.ts:153`.
- `src/lib/aiServices.ts` has 22 `console.*` calls in shipped code paths. AGENTS.md bans these.
- `docs/architecture/README.md:68` (roadmap item 9) proposes an `AudienceOracle` port in front of Gemini and the fallback.

## How to reproduce
Key leak (read the code path):
1. Put `VITE_GEMINI_API_KEY=test-key-123` in `.env`.
2. Run `npm run build`, then `grep -r test-key-123 dist/`. The key is in the bundle.

Guessable audience:
1. Reach a faction audience on the survivor path, either in play or with the balance sim's stubs (`scripts/simulate-campaign.ts:24-25`).
2. Answer A, A, A.
3. The outcome is always `victory`. The same goes for B, B, B on shadow-ruler.

## Suggested fix
- Delete the Gemini path completely: `callAI`, `buildQuestionPrompt`, `buildJudgmentPrompt`, `parseQuestions`, `parseOutcome`, the schemas and `AI_CONFIG`. Drop the `VITE_GEMINI_API_KEY` mention from AGENTS.md "Known hazards".
- Make the audience synchronous and pure. Something like `drawAudience({ path, rng }) → AudienceQuestion[]` and `judgeAudience({ path, questions, answers, gameContext }) → { outcome, message }`, with the result returned and no network call. The audience machine can then drop `fromPromise`, the `onError` branch and the 30s timeout. Replace the old path, don't layer on it: no "AI if available" branch.
- Keep one `getFallbackQuestions` (or its replacement) in one module, and delete the copy.
- Make the answers non-guessable:
  - Author a bank of questions per path (more than three each) and draw three with the seeded campaign RNG. Never use `Math.random`.
  - Shuffle the option order per question with the same RNG, so the right letter changes from run to run.
  - Consider letting the context bonus matter even at 3/3, e.g. require some loyalty or influence for victory, so knowing the answers alone isn't enough. Balance is the owner's call; check it with `node --import tsx scripts/simulate-campaign.ts 100 1 60`.

Replace the `FALLBACK_QUESTIONS` stubs in `tests/gameMachine.test.ts`, `tests/campaignSave.test.ts` and `scripts/simulate-campaign.ts` with the new interface.
