title: Game machine pops blocking alert() boxes and hides gameplay notices in console.log
body:
## What happens
- Five game events pop a native browser `alert()` box. It freezes the page, including the 3D palace render loop, until you dismiss it, and it looks nothing like the palace UI.
- After a Spit in Face, the knock-on suspicion for other courtiers lands 100ms later from a `setTimeout`, outside the machine transition, and then fires an `alert()`.
- The witness fallout from a gift (rebels seeing an ambitious gift, loyal witnesses rewarding a loyal one) reaches only `console.log`. The player never learns that witnesses changed their suspicion.
- The machine also logs debug noise (faction offers, faction bonuses, Emperor audience results) with `console.log`/`console.warn`. This breaks AGENTS.md rule 5 and the "no `console.log` or `alert` in shipped code paths" style rule.

## Where
All in `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts`:
- `:666`: `FACTION_MEMBERSHIP_OFFERED` → `alert(\`The ${event.faction} faction has offered you membership! ...\`)`
- `:735`: faction join result → `alert(message)` ("You have joined the ... faction! Gained support with: ...")
- `:836-880`: `SPIT_IN_FACE` action wraps everything in `setTimeout(() => { ... }, 100)`. Inside it, `applyCrossCharacterEffects` (`src/lib/crossCharacterEffects.ts:162`) sends `APPLY_SUSPICION_CHANGE` to other actors, then `:872` `console.log(...)` and `:873` `alert(crossCharacterNotification)`.
- `:1053-1055`: `GIVE_EMPEROR_GIFT` in `emperor_encounter`. You can't afford the tribute, `emperor_loyalty_bypass` passes, and you get `alert("Your perceived loyalty saves you from execution.")`
- `:1070-1072`: `REFUSE` with the same bypass, same `alert`
- `:543-546`: witness note from `generateCrossCharacterNotification`, only `console.log(note)` with a comment `// optional UI surface`
- More machine logging: `:690`, `:695`, `:699`, `:705`, `:710`, `:714`, `:721`, `:877`, `:1000`, `:1002`, `:1006`, `:1009`, `:1300-1303`, `:1348-1350`

Side effects:
- About 15 test files (for example `tests/gameMachine.test.ts:15`, `tests/courtGraph.test.ts:8`, `tests/tributeRanks.test.ts:14`) stub `globalThis.alert` and mock `console.log` only so the machine can run under node.
- `docs/architecture/README.md` roadmap item 3 ("Side effects out of the machine") already names this.

## How to reproduce
1. Start a campaign and win support from 3 members of one faction, then advance the season. An `alert()` box announces the faction offer.
2. Join the faction. A second `alert()` lists the support and suspicion changes.
3. Spit in Face at a courtier who has allies present. About 100ms later a third `alert()` lists the cross-character suspicion.
4. During an Emperor encounter, refuse (or present with too few gifts for the tribute) while your reputation is high enough for the loyalty bypass. You get an `alert()` pardon.
5. Give an ambitious gift with rebels in the zone, and open devtools. The witness suspicion note shows up only in the console.

## Suggested fix
- Add one notices module (`src/lib/notices.ts`) that owns the notice type and pure helpers such as `pushNotice(notices, notice) → notices` and `ackNotices(notices, ids) → notices`. Keep it bounded, with stable ids like `${season}:${seq}`.
- Store `notices` in campaign context. Replace each `alert()` and the witness `console.log` with an `assign` that pushes a notice. Add an `ACK_NOTICES` event.
- Render notices in React as toasts using the theme (`src/ui/`), with `playCue` where it fits. Point the existing header notifications button at a minimal notices list until the Chronicle tab exists.
- Drop the Spit in Face `setTimeout`. Compute the cross-character effects in the same transition from the target's current snapshot, send the suspicion changes to the actors there, and push a notice. Then the effects land in one transition and a save straight after includes them.
- Delete the debug `console.log`/`console.warn` calls rather than routing them anywhere.
- Replace, don't layer: once the machine stops calling `alert`, remove the `globalThis.alert` stubs and `console.log` mocks from the tests. Add machine tests through `createActor`: each of the five events produces a notice in context and makes no `alert` call, and Spit in Face fallout is visible right after the event with no timer.
- Needs no new `useEffect`/`useMemo`/`useCallback`. If a toast timer seems to need one, ask the owner first.

## Related
- Slice 2a: Notices (split out of Slice 2: Real presents by the red-team review). Tracked in #2.
- `docs/architecture/README.md` deepening roadmap item 3.

title: Tribute outcome is never shown: tributeResult is written and saved but no UI reads it
body:
## What happens
- The player pays tribute when the Emperor calls. The game rolls whether the Emperor favors it, with a 30% chance of +4 influence points.
- The outcome text ("The Emperor favors your tribute. Influence +N." or "The Emperor receives your tribute without comment.") goes into campaign context and the save. No screen ever shows it.
- The encounter view closes right after payment. The player can't tell whether the roll hit unless they open "Your court" and compare the influence number from memory.

## Where
- `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:1039-1045`: the `GIVE_EMPEROR_GIFT` tribute branch draws from the seeded RNG and sets the text:
  ```ts
  tributeResult:favored?`The Emperor favors your tribute. Influence +${gain}.`:'The Emperor receives your tribute without comment.'
  ```
- `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:1021-1025`: `after_emperor` has only `always` transitions to `advancing_season` or `in_season`. Nothing stops to show a result.
- `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:243`: the field's type. It gets initial values at `:159`, `:365` and `:1127`. It is never cleared after a tribute, so the text from the last tribute sits in context until the next one.
- `src/persistence/campaignSave.ts:144`: the save validator checks `tributeResult`, so it is saved with every campaign.
- `src/components/GameLayout.tsx:229`: the only Emperor-encounter UI hook. It checks `playing.emperor_encounter`, which is already over by the time `tributeResult` is set.
- No file in `src/components/`, `src/palace/` or `src/ui/` references `tributeResult` (`grep -rn tributeResult src`).
- `src/lib/campaignBalance.ts:39-40`: `tributeFavorChance: 0.30`, `tributeInfluenceReward: 0.04`.
- For comparison, `careerNotice` is rendered as a status line at `src/components/GameLayout.tsx:472`.

## How to reproduce
1. Start a campaign and play into season 2 or later with enough gifts for tribute.
2. When the Emperor's encounter appears, pay tribute.
3. The encounter closes and play continues. No message says whether the Emperor favored the tribute.
4. Read the code path: `grep -rn tributeResult src` only finds hits in the machine and the save validator.

## Suggested fix
- Preferred (replace, don't layer): when the notices module from Slice 2 lands, have the tribute branch return a notice through `pushNotice` and delete `tributeResult` from context, the save validator and the schema. Map any saved value into a notice in the migration. Show a favored tribute with `<PopNumber>` on influence and a `playCue('chime')`. Show the neutral result as a quiet notice.
- If this needs fixing before Slice 2: render `context.tributeResult` as a `role="status"` line, the same way `careerNotice` is rendered at `GameLayout.tsx:472`. Clear it on the next player action or season change, so the text never goes stale. Keep the roll in the machine on `nextCampaignRandom`. Don't add a `useEffect` to auto-dismiss it without the owner's approval.
- Add a `createActor` machine test that gives a seeded RNG state, sends `GIVE_EMPEROR_GIFT` and checks the emitted result for both the favored and the neutral outcome. Add a render test showing that the result text appears in the UI.

## Related
- Slice 2: Real presents (the `src/lib/notices.ts` module that replaces scattered notice fields). Part of #2.
- Slice 8: The Night of Slips and the Emperor's scenes, which turns tribute into a full scene. The tribute outcome should be a visible beat of that scene.

title: Assets: one shared animation-only emote GLB for conversations
body:
> Part of #2 · Slice ASSETS · Size L · Depends on: nothing for art; #4 for conversation integration

## What changes for the player

- Courtiers bow, speak, whisper, laugh and scoff during conversations.
- Talk has two restrained gesture variations, suited to an elegant imperial palace.
- Kneeling and presenting an item get their own authored gestures.
- Each gesture blends back into the courtier's normal pose without moving their palace position.
- Conversations keep working while the animation file is loading or unavailable.

## Why

- A JSON-chunk audit of all 84 current `public/models/**/*.glb` files found no Bow, Talk, Whisper, Laugh, Scoff or Kneel clips and zero morph targets. Existing clips cover locomotion, jumps, gifts and the Emperor's idle/approach.
- The loader currently selects idle, walk, run and gift/reaction clips at `src/palace/characterModels.ts:151`; its public reaction entry points are at `src/palace/characterModels.ts:203` and `src/palace/characterModels.ts:214`.
- Existing cast files have exact cache fingerprints and clip-list locks: `tests/castRegistry.test.ts:4`, `tests/castRegistry.test.ts:7`, `tests/castRegistry.test.ts:33` and `tests/castRegistry.test.ts:40`. A separate animation file preserves those contracts.

## Scope

1. **Owner decision before production.** Choose commission or in-house production, name the producer, and agree on budget, delivery date and usage rights. Record the decision in this issue. Asset spending requires the owner's OK. #4 can ship its procedural gestures while this work is pending.

2. **Deliver an artist brief and editable source.** Use the existing 63-joint rig as the authoring reference, for example `public/models/player-concubine.glb`. Preserve its body-bone names, hierarchy, rest pose and local axes. Produce one animation-only GLB at `public/models/court-emotes.glb`, with an editable source file and a provenance/manifest document. Export armature nodes and animation data; exclude character meshes, textures and materials.

3. **Author these eight clips.** Use the exact names below. Record actual duration, looping and blend recommendations in the manifest; normalize each exported clip to start at time zero.

   | Clip | Direction | Playback |
   |---|---|---|
   | `Bow` | Measured palace courtesy; head and torso carry the gesture | One shot; return to rest |
   | `Talk_A` | Small open-handed explanation | Seamless loop |
   | `Talk_B` | Quieter, distinct conversational emphasis | Seamless loop |
   | `Whisper` | Discreet lean and hand gesture | Seamless loop |
   | `Laugh` | Brief, restrained amusement | One shot; return to rest |
   | `Scoff` | Cool dismissal, readable through head and shoulders | One shot; return to rest |
   | `Kneel` | Formal lowering and recovery, tested after export | One shot; return to rest |
   | `Present` | Two-handed offering, with empty hands | One shot; return to rest |

   Keep gestures readable in the medium conversation shots from #4. Facial animation, lip sync, new morph targets and gift-object meshes are outside this slice. Inspect Kneel after translation stripping; if its ground contact fails, return the revised gesture proposal to the owner before accepting the art.

4. **Validate the export against the real rig families.** The current binary audit found:

   | Joints | Current family | Files |
   |---|---|---|
   | 63 | Concubine/consort/maid bases; three concubine player ranks; all scoped maids; scoped Concubine Mei | 23 |
   | 59 | Other NPC bases, Prince Feng runtime, all scoped eunuchs, all 18 scoped-t2 scholar variants | 51 |
   | 57 | Emperor, legacy Maid Ling, all prince player ranks and all scholar player ranks | 8 |

   Two further GLBs are unskinned furniture. The scoped-t2 59-joint files are scholars in this checkout; prince player files have 57 joints. Re-run the inventory before export acceptance, since additional art may land in parallel.

   All 82 skinned files share 53 body-bone names, including `head`, `neck_01` and `spine_02`. The 63-joint authoring rig covers the shared body; accessory bones differ between families. Strip every animation translation channel and every `sleeve_drape_*`, `cloth_*` and `hair_*` track. Export rotation channels only for shared body bones; leave `Root` unanimated. Do not animate the 57-joint family's `robe_*` accessories. Preserve static rest translations on the armature nodes.

5. **Add the runtime binding in one place.** Extend `loadCourtCharacterModels` with `play(name, emote | null)`, where `emote` is the union of the eight clip names and `@player` identifies the player. `null` stops the emote and restores the normal pose. Hide loading, bone-name binding, loop rules, interruption and crossfades behind this interface. Load the shared file lazily on first use through the existing `ModelAssetPool`; give it its own content fingerprint. Keep character asset URL enumeration unchanged.

   Bind tracks to each actor's existing skeleton by bone name. Never bind by source node index or UUID, attach the source armature to the palace, or mutate shared clip templates. Check rest-pose compatibility on each family; put any required rotation-basis conversion inside this binding module. Keep each actor's mixer and action state independent, following `src/palace/assetPool.ts:131`.

   Retain `react`/`reactPlayer` and their gift fallback for existing callers. An unavailable emote returns to the #4 procedural gesture or the existing gift clip. Emote loading failure must leave player readiness and ordinary character art usable. Disposal cancels pending work and releases the emote lease and action bindings, following `src/palace/assetPool.ts:167`.

6. **Connect to #4 once ready.** Trigger Talk_A/B while a line is spoken; stop it when the line or scene ends. Reaction beats choose Laugh, Scoff, Whisper or Present explicitly. Trigger Bow/Kneel only from their authored beats. Use the existing frame loop for playback. Scenes may animate while movement input is locked; menus and hidden tabs freeze animation time. Preserve jump and movement priority when the player leaves a scene. Software rendering uses no-op `play` and performs no emote download.

7. **Record acceptance evidence.** Publish the GLB checksum, clip metadata, rig inventory, source/provenance and WebGL recordings of every clip on 63-, 59- and 57-joint representatives. Check the Emperor separately: its dedicated loader and mixer live at `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:182`. Reuse the same binding logic when an Emperor scene requests an emote; retain its Imperial_Idle/Imperial_Approach behavior and lazy loading.

## Delete in the same PR

- Replace any per-family copies of the new emote animations with the single shared file before merge.
- Remove duplicated clip-binding or playback helpers introduced during production.
- Replace the procedural gesture on the successful authored-emote path; keep one explicit loading/failure fallback so both gestures never run together.
- Leave existing cast GLBs, their clip lists and fingerprints intact. The existing Gift_Present fallback remains necessary.

## New or changed modules

- `public/models/court-emotes.glb`: the single animation payload; eight named clips on the authoring armature.
- `public/models/court-emotes-manifest.json` and an editable source/provenance document: checksum, producer, rights, reference rig, durations, loop modes and export restrictions.
- `src/palace/characterModels.ts`: owns `play(name, emote | null)`, action priority, restoration and fallback.
- `src/palace/characterEmotes.ts`, if needed: owns loading and binding shared clips to an existing actor root. Both courtier/player playback and the separate Emperor loader use it; callers never filter tracks themselves.
- `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx`: scene-beat wiring, software no-op and Emperor integration within its existing lifetime/frame loop.
- Reuse `src/palace/assetPool.ts:30`; add no parallel asset cache or new animation mixer per gesture.

## Tests

- Add `tests/characterEmotes.test.ts`: parse the delivered GLB as asset data; assert eight exact names, positive finite durations, time-zero starts, rotation-only shared-body targets, no accessory/Root animation, and no meshes, materials or images.
- Bind and advance all eight clips through the public emote interface on real 63/59/57 rigs. Assert valid finite bone transforms, expected gesture motion and unchanged palace root position, yaw and scale. Shuffle source node order in a fixture to prove name binding.
- Test two actors playing different emotes independently, repeated one-shots, loop cancellation, return to idle, scene exit and jump/movement priority. Assert the shared source clips remain unchanged.
- Extend `tests/assetLifecycle.test.ts` with first-use sharing, abort during download/decode, repeated zone changes and idempotent disposal. Assert no emote lease or late attachment survives disposal.
- Extend `tests/modelLoading.test.ts` with missing/malformed emote-file fallback. Keep emote failures separate from character readiness; no extra download occurs until `play` requests one.
- No existing test file needs deletion or replacement if the old interface and lazy-loading contract are preserved. Retain `tests/castRegistry.test.ts`, `tests/princePlayerModel.test.ts`, `tests/modelLoading.test.ts`, `tests/assetLifecycle.test.ts` and `tests/playtestMode.test.ts`.
- `tests/castRegistry.test.ts` reads GLB asset data and hashes; keep those checks. Add behavior tests through the new interface; avoid source/CSS regex assertions.

## Save impact

- None. Gestures, clip time, loading state and mixer state remain presentation state.
- Do not add machine states, consume campaign RNG, change court graph results or alter existing character identity hashes.

## Review notes to handle

- **Rig correction:** use the verified 63/59/57 families above. Author on 63 joints and bind only shared body bones; strip translations and sleeve, cloth and hair tracks before delivery.
- **Owner process:** commissioning/production is an unresolved owner decision. This issue records the proposed contract; it authorizes no spending.
- **Separate asset contract:** the Emperor has only Imperial_Idle/Imperial_Approach; its current file is 18,056,168 bytes. Keep that file and the cast clip/hash locks unchanged.
- **Presentation limits:** shared bone names establish a binding route; they do not prove equivalent silhouettes or rest axes. WebGL cross-rig inspection is required. Keep mobile and software navigation usable throughout.

## Hooks that need the owner's OK

- None expected. Use the existing PalaceScene lifetime, live props and frame loop for requests, completion, freeze and disposal.
- If implementation requires a new effect, memo, callback or subscription, list it and its frame-loop/ref alternative for owner approval before adding it.

## How to check it

1. After the owner chooses the production route, review the eight-clip preview and source/provenance delivery.
2. In WebGL, start a concubine game. Speak to a courtier and inspect both talk loops, then the authored reaction and courtesy beats. Leave mid-loop and check that walking resumes normally.
3. Repeat with scholar and prince players and a 59-joint courtier. Use a development-only clip selector if normal story beats do not expose all eight clips yet; keep it out of the shipped HUD.
4. Inspect bow, kneel and present from front and side on all three rig families, including the Emperor. Check feet, robe/sleeve clipping, head turns and smooth recovery.
5. Open a menu and hide the tab mid-emote. Resume, change zones repeatedly, and change the player's rank outfit. Check independent actors and absence of stale gestures.
6. Block the emote request and repeat a conversation: the fallback remains usable. Open `?renderer=software` and check navigation with no emote-file request.
7. Repeat a conversation on a phone-sized WebGL viewport and with reduced motion enabled. Keep gestures restrained and the existing animation/frame budget intact.

## Done when

- The owner has recorded commission/production, budget and rights decisions.
- One accepted eight-clip animation-only GLB, editable source and manifest are delivered.
- Cross-rig playback and loading/fallback/disposal tests pass; existing cast fingerprints and clip lists remain unchanged.
- `npm run check` and `npm run build` pass.
- You loaded the game and looked at the change in WebGL; all eight clips have cross-rig visual evidence.
- Code review done with GPT-6.1 Sol via T3 `delegate_task` (owner's rule).

title: S11: Bring court happenings and the remaining 38 courtiers to life
body:
> Part of #2 · Slice S11 · Size XL · Depends on: #8, #11, #12, #13, #15

## What changes for the player

- Step into a quarrel under the plum tree. Side with either courtier, soothe them, or walk away.
- Hear a guqin recital, meet its audience, and face a rival who approaches with a pointed remark.
- Notice secret meetings tied to real plots. Seasonal festivals warm the lanterns and scatter gold petals.
- Learn distinct tastes, voices and optional favours for the remaining 38 courtiers.
- Build a bond with each of the 20 tier-3/4 courtiers to uncover a three-beat personal story.

## Why

- The current reply bank has six outcomes with three shared lines each and picks through `Math.random`: `src/lib/getResponse.ts:2`, `src/lib/getResponse.ts:37`. #8 replaces it; S11 finishes the personal writing.
- The roster has 48 persistent names across 12 offices: `src/lib/courtHierarchy.ts:3`, `tests/courtHierarchy.test.ts:7`. Office defaults alone leave most people interchangeable.
- Only 12–16 courtiers are in residence each season: `src/lib/campaignBalance.ts:14`. Scenes must work with actual presence and empty rooms.
- Three hundred lines cannot cover the full court, player replies, favours, rumours and stories. Fund and measure 3,000+ authored lines across the completed reimagining.

## Scope

1. Land the content manifest, coverage command and happening rules before the writing PRs.
   - Preserve the 48 names, office costs, careers, promotion targets and existing plot cadence.
   - Reuse #8 voice selection, #11 rumours, #12 favour budgets and #15 continuous presence.
   - Treat module paths below as proposed additions or extensions. They describe the implementation after those dependencies land.
2. Plan happenings once per zone/watch with `campaignStream(campaignSeed, season, purpose)`.
   - Include zone/watch in the purpose key. Sort eligible names before casting. Reuse the immutable seed introduced by #7.
   - Allow at most one happening per zone/watch. Persist its cast and completion so reload or re-entry cannot reroll it.
   - Quarrel: two living, co-present courtiers with a directed hate edge of at least 30, at a reachable plum-tree or equivalent authored spot.
   - Recital: a present performer at a guqin spot plus up to three present listeners. Skip when casting or access fails.
   - Interception: a present hostile courtier approaches through the director. Show an interaction prompt; the player chooses whether to speak.
   - Secret meeting: use an existing pending plot and present participants. Feed its true facts into Listen; never invent a plot or reveal inaccessible participants.
   - Festival: a cosmetic event every third season in the Horse watch. Recolour existing lanterns and play a bounded gold burst. No support, influence, taels or items.
   - Prefer festivals on their scheduled watch; defer other candidates. Skip invalid casts without spawning substitute named actors.
3. Add `SOCIAL_ACT` intervention through the shared social transaction handler from #7.
   - Request includes happening ID, choice ID, request ID, watch and the same witness snapshot shown before commitment.
   - Side with A: +2 support from A to the player and -2 from B; side with B reverses them.
   - Soothe: reduce each existing directed hate edge between the pair by 4, floored at zero. No player support award.
   - Extend the canonical relationship reducer with a bounded hate-reduction command; its current `hate` command accepts increases only: `src/lib/courtGraph.ts:56`. Never patch graph edges in the UI.
   - Positive intervention support shares #12's per-courtier, per-season favour allowance, capped at Proper. Consume the payout opportunity; never add a second free reward channel.
   - Show consequences in words before commitment. Take your leave has no effect. Invalid, stale or repeated requests change nothing.
   - Route graph commands, actor projections, suspicion and notices through the established handler. Rules never pay global support awards.
4. Split writing into seven per-office content PRs, each reviewed against the same style and coverage rules.

| Content PR | Names owned by S11 | Minimum new authored strings |
|---|---|---:|
| Maids | Ling, Su, Bai, Lan, Ting, He, Rou, Zhu | 250 |
| Eunuchs | Gao, Lu, Ren, Min, Jin, Bo, Tian, Shu | 250 |
| Scholars | Qin, Tao, Jia, Ren, Song, Yu | 250 |
| Princes | Feng, Han, Jun, Lei | 200 |
| Ministers | Chen, Wang, Liu, Zhang | 200 |
| Generals | Zhao, Shen, Wei, Luo | 200 |
| Senior figures | Empress Dowager, Empress Consort, Crown Prince, Prime Minister | 250 |

   - The #8 ten are Concubines Mei, Lin, Xia, Yun, An, Qiao and Consorts Hua, Zhen, Rong, Yue. Maid He remains in S11's eight-maid group even if she received an earlier cameo.
   - Each of the remaining 38 gets a signature love, a signature loathe, personal greeting/reaction/taste-hint lines, contextual written replies and at least one complete optional favour script.
   - Per-person floors: eight personal lines, six player reply lines and offer/complete/expire favour lines. Office-pack coverage is additional.
   - Voice rules: restrained palace speech, concrete objects, brief dry humour and personal stakes. Use “this servant” or “this palace” where rank warrants it. Avoid modern slang, repeated platitudes and fixed stance trios.
   - Let office and biography shape speech; factions still follow rolled traits and graph facts. Write pronouns and address for every applicable career.
   - Loves and loathes must reference items at or above the courtier's tier under the existing etiquette-first resolver. Coverage must execute the resolver to prove the intended taste wins.
   - Hints enter Brush Notes as suspected. Confirmed entries cite the deciding rule and actual source; under-grade rejection cannot confirm a loathe.
5. Complete all voice packs and existing content families, with an explicit budget ledger.

| Content family | Slice owner | Budget by S11 |
|---|---|---:|
| Ladies' Court personal dialogue and replies | #8 | 300+ strings |
| Item blurbs | #7 | About 36 |
| Rumour and scheme text | #11, #14 if approved | 60+ |
| Lore slips, lost-item captions and initial favour scripts | #12 | 100+; includes 40–60 lore slips |
| Career-specific audience banks | #13 | 45+ |
| Seven office content PRs above | S11 | 1,600+ new strings |
| Shared office/temperament packs, all slots and five bond bands | #8 + S11 | 2,250+ strings; expand to the actual matrix size |
| Twenty personal arcs, including the four consorts | S11 | 180+ strings |
| Happening dialogue, choices and reactions | S11 | 90+ strings |

   - These are writing estimates and floors, not a reason to pad. Report unique non-empty player-facing strings and resolved coverage cells separately.
   - Count shared packs once. Imports, whitespace, duplicated lines and filling many cells with one generic line do not increase authored volume.
   - The realistic budget exceeds 3,000 lines. Adjust the ledger upward when the actual office × temperament × slot × band matrix requires it.
   - Every supported matrix cell must resolve through its personal or office pack. Report generic fallback as missing production coverage.
   - Keep all 48 names playable during intermediate PRs. Each PR gates its own office; the final PR gates the whole court.
6. Write three-beat arcs for all 20 tier-3/4 courtiers.
   - Counts: four each of prince, minister, general and consort, plus the four senior figures: `src/lib/courtHierarchy.ts:8`.
   - Unlock successive beats at Trusted, Confidante and Sworn using the existing bond-band selector. Read canonical support; do not add a second relationship meter.
   - Beat one reveals a private concern; beat two asks for a contextual choice or existing favour; beat three resolves that concern and recalls the choice.
   - Persist completion and choices. Never replay rewards after reload. Temporary absence pauses access; death or expulsion ends availability without resurrecting anyone.
   - Reveal knowledge or character history. Any support or item reward must use the existing favour payout and supply budget. No new promotion requirement.
7. Integrate through the existing scene, interaction stack, barks and director.
   - Reserve engaged participants through #15. Release reservations on exit, completion, watch change or participant loss; preserve ordinary departures.
   - At most 10 animated actors per zone, including performers, audiences and extras. Happenings reuse the present roster.
   - Throttle mixers beyond 15 m or offscreen; disable cast shadows beyond 12 m. Drop extras and festival particles on struggling coarse-pointer devices.
   - Use lacquer plaques, silk subtitles, theme tokens, Emblem glyphs and `playCue`. Reuse separate #17 emotes when available; procedural look-at and existing clips remain the fallback.
   - No new asset commission, forced procession, errand board or permanent favour tracker. Update the architecture map and glossary for Happenings and Personal stories.

## Delete in the same PR

- Replace remaining office-default-only taste entries and placeholder personal lines for each office as its content PR lands.
- Remove superseded fallback favour scripts and duplicate taste/voice tables. Keep one owner for each concept.
- Remove temporary coverage exclusions as offices finish. Generic fallback may handle invalid/debug inputs but cannot satisfy production coverage.

title: S10: Walk in, walk out: stop rebuilding rooms when courtiers change watch
body:
> Part of #2 · Slice S10 · Size XL · Depends on: #10, #11, #12, #13

## What changes for the player

- At the watch drum, courtiers leave through doors and new faces walk to their places.
- The room, camera and player stay steady while the court changes around them.
- A courtier finishes speaking with you before leaving.
- The watch name and drum remain. The ink-wash loading curtain disappears.
- Saving and returning preserves a courtier's place and facing.

## Why

- Fixes #27: `rosterKey` is a world-construction dependency at `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:448`.
- A roster change runs full cleanup at `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:446`, then recreates the world and camera at `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:125` and `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:154`.
- Presence currently publishes scheduled names at `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:456`; it cannot describe people still walking out or waiting to enter.
- Character loading captures its targets once at `src/palace/characterModels.ts:112`. Individual arrivals and departures need their own lifetime.

## Scope

Implement in these commits. The director and authored spots come from #10; extend those modules rather than creating another runtime.

1. **Make roster changes an in-place director operation.**
   - Remove `rosterKey` from the construction effect's dependencies after the update path is wired.
   - Keep intentional replacement when the player changes zone, role or campaign visit-state identity.
   - Compare the latest desired roster with director-owned residents by canonical courtier name.
   - Call `syncRoster(arrivals, departures)` after committed input changes; repeated identical inputs do nothing.
   - Existing residents retain their spatial roots, models, facing and current paths. Replan only changed intents.
   - Never recreate the renderer, room geometry, player, camera, input listeners or Emperor rig for a roster update.

2. **Walk through the correct gate.**
   - Use the gate leading to the destination zone for departures, and the reciprocal gate from the previous zone for arrivals.
   - The existing topology is all-to-all: `src/palace/zones.ts:26` supplies destination-labelled gates.
   - Use reachable thresholds inside the bounds and the existing navigator. The doors are interaction boundaries; walking beyond a blocked wall is unnecessary.
   - Acquire an arrival's model before its visible entrance. Start it at the gate threshold and walk to its assigned authored spot.
   - A departing resident remains visible and present until reaching its exit threshold; then remove its spatial root and release its model.
   - If an active courtier has no previous zone, use a deterministic entry gate. Never place a new arrival directly at its final spot.
   - Queue entrances when the animation budget is full. Navigation and presence remain correct for every resident.
   - A new watch supersedes pending travel by name. Cancel obsolete arrivals; redirect or cancel departures without duplicate roots or leases.
   - Casualties and expulsions cancel travel and remove the affected courtier immediately; they never receive a later arrival callback.

3. **Publish physical presence and hold the engaged partner.**
   - Return gate-crossing changes from `step(dt, mode)`; the scene adapter sends a full, deduplicated `UPDATE_PALACE_PRESENCE` list.
   - In WebGL, arrivals become present after their model is ready and they cross inward. Departures remain present until crossing outward.
   - In software QA, the same crossing rules use spatial anchors without model loading.
   - Feed target guards, local minimap dots, interaction candidates and spatial witnesses from this actual population.
   - Keep schedule data as destination intent. Do not overwrite local physical presence with `zoneRoster` at each watch.
   - Hold an engaged partner in place while dialogue is open; after leave, walk toward the latest scheduled destination.
   - Preserve #11's witness commitment policy. If witnesses were frozen on scene entry, keep that exact list through preview and receipt.
   - Publish initial presence when the scene is ready and revalidate it after a season reset even if no names changed.
   - The machine clears presence at `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:949`; its update handler filters active names at `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:487`.
   - Preserve those guards. A stale async crossing must never publish into a different zone or restored campaign.

4. **Give each spatial courtier a complete lifetime.**
   - Add per-name acquire/remove operations to `characterModels`; removal aborts pending work and disposes an attached instance with its mixer.
   - Keep private skeletons and shared template art through `acquireModelInstance`. Its instance disposal releases the pool lease at `src/palace/assetPool.ts:176`.
   - Preserve stale-request protection at `src/palace/characterModels.ts:132`; cover removal followed by re-entry during fetch or decode.
   - Retry only current failed targets. A failed arrival stays outside presence; it does not block ready residents or replace them with primitive bodies.
   - Replace index-based labels with courtier-name ownership. The current projection assumes `labels[i]` matches `world.npcs[i]` at `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:394`.
   - Remove the root, ring, label, bark, interaction candidate, look-at and reaction references together.
   - Dispose the whole director on zone teardown; every in-flight acquire and callback belongs to that director generation.

5. **Remove the mask and finish persistence.**
   - Delete #10's watch-only ink-wash mask, its timer, completion callbacks and pause flag. Keep the watch name and drum without blocking movement.
   - Preserve demotion acknowledgments, season settlement and #13's Emperor ceremonies; they carry campaign behavior.
   - Persist optional `spotId` beside each NPC pose, including periodic capture and teardown capture.
   - Complete the v11 migration and validators below before changing emitted saves.
   - Update the architecture documentation with the director's ownership of roster lifetime and physical presence.

## Delete in the same PR

- The roster-triggered room teardown path and scheduled-name presence effect.
- Fixed initial-target bookkeeping replaced by per-name character registration.
- Index-owned NPC labels and duplicate arrival/departure cleanup paths.
- The watch loading mask and its exclusive styles. Delete obsolete legacy rules; add no new legacy CSS.
- Any obsolete rebuild assumptions in tests. Preserve intentional player zone changes and campaign restart cleanup.

## New or changed modules

| Module | Interface and ownership |
|---|---|
| `src/lib/courtLife.ts` | Pure planning with schedule, previous locations and authored spots as inputs; returns travel intents. Hides gate choice and deterministic spot assignment. Consumes no campaign RNG. |
| `src/palace/courtLifeDirector.ts` | Extend `apply`, `syncRoster`, `step`, `positions`, `dispose`. Hides travel queues, engaged holds, gate thresholds and per-name lifetimes; returns crossing results. |
| `src/palace/characterModels.ts` | Per-name add/remove plus existing readiness, retry and update operations. Hides async cancellation, private skeletons, mixers and model leases. |
| `src/palace/assetPool.ts` | Reuse `acquireModelInstance` and idempotent `dispose`; extend only if a demonstrated lifecycle defect requires it. |
| `src/palace/world.ts` | Extend #10's spatial registration/removal boundary so the director can change residents without rebuilding architecture. |
| `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx` | Own committed roster delivery, frame stepping, keyed labels, HUD telemetry and presence-event forwarding. |
| `src/palace/zones.ts`, `src/persistence/campaignSave.ts` | Own the shared pose type, save v11, migration and validation. |

## Tests

Use public interfaces, fake asset fetch/decode and deterministic director steps. Never regex-match source or CSS.

- Add/extend `tests/courtLifeDirector.test.ts` from #10: arrivals reach spots; departures reach their destination gate and disappear after bounded steps.
- Assert repeated `syncRoster` is idempotent, engaged departure waits for leave, changed destinations cancel old travel, and `worldFrozen` halts travel.
- Assert presence changes exactly at crossings, initial/season revalidation occurs, and stale callbacks cannot affect another zone.
- Add a machine integration case in `tests/gameMachine.test.ts`: target unavailable before arrival, available while resident/departing, unavailable after exit; guards still reject casualties.
- Repeated watch cycles preserve room/player identities and return to the expected object, label and lease counts after travel settles; teardown returns owned leases to zero.
- Test removal during fetch/decode, immediate re-entry, failed arrival retry, shared-template survival and idempotent teardown.
- Replace affected assumptions in these existing suites; retain unrelated coverage:
  - `tests/assetLifecycle.test.ts`: fixed-roster setup becomes dynamic roster cycles with independent animation state and exact lease cleanup.
  - `tests/modelLoading.test.ts`: retain cancellation/readiness cases; add individual departure/re-entry without whole-world disposal.
  - `tests/palaceZones.test.ts`: replace NPC rebuild recovery with v11 pose/spot restoration and in-place roster identity checks; keep zone architecture/disposal checks.
  - `tests/palaceSchedules.test.ts`, `tests/ladiesResidences.test.ts`: replace any remaining route-stop or immediate scheduled-spawn assumptions with reachable gate-to-spot journeys through the director.
  - `tests/campaignSave.test.ts`, `tests/campaignSaveMigration.test.ts`: extend pose round trips and migration coverage to optional `spotId` and transitional recovery.
  - `tests/demotionNotice.test.ts`: if shared transition wiring changes, use render and actor tests for acknowledgment; delete the affected source-regex assertions.
- Keep `tests/assetPool.test.ts` green. Keep `tests/emperorEntrance.test.ts` and #13's scene tests green; add roster churn during an Emperor entrance with one arrival acknowledgment and no extra lease.
- Extend #11's witness tests and #9's HUD tests so local dots/candidates follow physical presence while committed witnesses follow the chosen scene policy.

## Save impact

- Schema v11, built on #12's v10 and intervening approved migrations. The current checkout is v7 at `src/persistence/campaignSave.ts:16`.
- Add `spotId?: PalaceSpotId` to `NpcVisitPose`; today's type is at `src/palace/zones.ts:6`.
- Older saves omit `spotId`; retain coordinates and facing, then assign a valid spot deterministically on restore. Migration leaves RNG, relationships, currency and clock unchanged.
- Validate a supplied spot against the authored registry and saved zone; reject unknown, wrong-zone or non-string values. Today's pose validation at `src/persistence/campaignSave.ts:71` does not check this field.
- Save physical poses while moving; transit queues, promises and engaged UI state remain transient.
- On reload, reconcile saved physical residents with the current desired roster, resume travel deterministically and publish actual presence before accepting actions. Stale poses from earlier visits do not create extra residents.
- Test v10-to-v11 golden migration, existing v7 golden fixtures through the full chain, v11 round trip, absent/invalid spots, and reload during arrival/departure without duplicated actors or awards.

## Review notes to handle

- **Hook pressure:** removing `rosterKey` alone freezes the initial population. Wire committed roster delivery before deleting that dependency; resolve the hook question below.
- **Placement:** choose spots relative to the actual entry gate, including side gates. Preserve spread across authored activities; avoid sorting everyone into the south cluster.
- **Witness drift:** moving people must not silently change a committed preview's witnesses. Carry forward and test #11's policy.
- **Procession frequency:** preserve the first visit plus approved rare events. An ordinary scheduled Emperor visit must not create a six-second cutscene every season.
- **Frame budget:** at most 10 animated actors per zone, including player, Emperor and animated extras. Throttle mixers beyond 15 m or offscreen; disable shadows beyond 12 m; retain low-FPS coarse-pointer extra suppression. Queue/throttle overlap during departures and arrivals.
- **Owner review process:** route implementation review to GPT-6.1 Sol through T3 `delegate_task` and address material findings before merge.

## Hooks that need the owner's OK

- **Decision required:** May `PalaceScene` use a committed roster-update `useEffect`, or repurpose its existing presence effect, to call `syncRoster` after roster/season/zone changes? It must not reconstruct the world.
- **Alternative without a new effect:** pass committed inputs into the existing runtime update path; the existing frame loop detects a changed roster generation and calls `syncRoster` before stepping. Initial mount synchronizes once; frozen worlds can reconcile inputs without advancing travel. Do not mutate the director during React render.
- Use the existing frame loop for travel, holds, mixer/shadow budgets and presence emissions; use existing telemetry for HUD updates. No new timers, subscriptions, `useMemo` or `useCallback` are expected.
- Record the owner's answer before implementing the effect route; the issue itself does not grant hook approval.

## How to check it

1. Start a concubine run in the Ladies' Court. Leave the camera pointed at a door through a watch drum; observe a departure and an arrival with no loading curtain or camera jump.
2. Approach an exiting courtier. Confirm they remain visible and interactable until departure, then disappear from local interaction choices and the minimap.
3. Open dialogue with a departing courtier using a deterministic QA setup. Confirm they wait, then walk out after you take your leave.
4. Enter through a side gate. Confirm arrivals use sensible doors and spread toward authored places rather than gathering at the south spawn.
5. Save during travel and reload. Confirm valid poses/facing, eventual destinations, and no duplicate courtiers. Repeat watch changes and zone backtracking; inspect lease/object telemetry for growth.
6. Repeat in `?playtest=1&renderer=software`: use the existing playtest console and spatial anchors to check routes and crossing presence. Character visuals require the separate WebGL pass.
7. Watch the Emperor's entrance during roster changes; check one arrival acknowledgment, lighting and scene camera. Check touch performance and reduced-motion mode.

- You loaded the game and looked at the change in WebGL and software QA.

title: S9: Schemes — turn rumours into leverage after the S6 playtest
body:
> Part of #2 · Slice S9 · Size L · Depends on: #11, #12, #13

## What changes for the player

- Confide a rumour to gain warmth and a favour owed.
- Spread a rumour to turn a listener against its subject. A devoted patron may turn against you.
- Threaten a plotter to cancel one warned plot. The resentment remains.
- Hush someone close to reporting you. A fearful courtier yields; a defiant one becomes more suspicious.
- Combine two matching rumour cards into Proof, then Expose their subject before named witnesses.

## Why

- Plots already grant a warning season, then consume pledged protectors before killing their target. Counterplay should use this cadence (`src/lib/courtPlots.ts:73`).
- An active plot survives equal influence. Expose must lower the attacker below the target, rather than promise safety at equality (`src/lib/courtPlots.ts:42`).
- Suspicion can trigger an immediate report through the actor. Current report limits are 1/3/5 for concubine/scholar/prince; follow the Q1 rule shipped by #13 (`src/state-machines/character-machine.ts:99`, `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:615`).
- One attacker can threaten several targets. Scheme actions must identify the full plot key (`src/lib/courtPlots.ts:26`).

## Scope

1. Record the owner's Q2 answer on this issue **after the owner plays #11**. This is an implementation gate.
   - A: rumours reveal information only. Close this slice without implementing scheme verbs.
   - B: implement Confide and Spread only; omit Threaten, Hush and Expose from rules, UI and content.
   - C: implement all five verbs. This is the plan's recommendation, pending the owner's answer.
   - Preserve the Q1 consequences already shipped by #13. This slice adds counterplay without choosing a new lethality rule.
2. Extend the #11 rumour book and `courtWhispers` interface. Keep one owner for cards, Proof, costs, eligibility and limits.
   - Cards retain stable IDs, subject, fact key, source speakers, spot, season and watch.
   - Proof requires two unspent cards about the same real fact and subject, from distinct successful Listen events.
   - Listening twice at one spot in one watch cannot supply both cards. For plot facts, include the full attacker/target key.
   - Combine the two cards atomically into one Proof card retaining both sources. Proof is spent once.
   - Keep the book bounded to 20 cards. Reject a combination of the same ID or unrelated facts.
3. Implement `rumourOptions(scene)` and `resolveRumour(scene, request)` with the initial rules below.
   - Request: `{verb, cardId, target, plotKey?, requestId, watch, witnesses}`. The conversational partner and rumour subject are distinct typed fields.
   - Options carry written labels, evidence, named witnesses, eligibility and a plain blocked reason.
   - Revalidate the card, current fact, living subject, reachable present partner, season, watch and limit at commit.
   - Rejected actions spend nothing. Accepted backfires spend the card and use the limit.
   - These magnitudes are starting tuning values from the proposals; put them together in one scheme balance table.

| Verb | Eligibility and committed result |
|---|---|
| Confide | Give a card about a third party to the listener. Consume it, set this watch's mood Warm, and record one favour owed by the listener through the #12 favour book. No immediate standing or taels. |
| Spread | Consume a card about subject S while speaking to L. Apply L → S hate +10 and S influence −0.05. If L is pledged to S, consume the card but apply L → player hate +10 instead; S receives no penalty. |
| Threaten | Speak to the card's subject and select a currently pending plot identified by its full key. Consume the card, apply subject → player hate +20 and suspicion +0.2, remove that one warning and record its cancellation. |
| Hush | Use a compromising, non-taste card on its unpledged subject in the near-report band defined by #11. Fear ≥0.5: suspicion −0.4. Fear <0.5: suspicion +0.3. Both consume the card and apply subject → player hate +20. |
| Expose | Consume Proof about S with at least two distinct named witnesses, excluding player and subject. Apply S influence −0.15 and S → player hate +30. Witnesses whose outgoing hate toward S is ≥60 gain +5 support toward the player through the normal relationship path. |

4. Bound use and preserve the existing court rules.
   - Confide: once per listener per season; at most one unredeemed favour owed by that listener.
   - Redeem that favour through #12's existing reward path, capped at Proper and its once-per-courtier-per-season payout. Include it in the same free-value budget; add no separate income path.
   - Spread, Threaten, Hush and Expose: each once per subject per season. Threaten still cancels only the selected plot.
   - Store limit keys and spent evidence durably. Changing zone, watch, scene or request ID cannot reset them.
   - Use `reduceCourtRelation` for every directed edge change; preserve pledge and faction hate immunity (`src/lib/courtGraph.ts:31`).
   - Clamp influence with `clampCourtInfluence`; clamp suspicion to [0,1] (`src/lib/courtHierarchy.ts:33`, `src/state-machines/character-machine.ts:67`).
   - Threaten grants no lasting immunity. A later season boundary can create a fresh warning with the full warning season. Leave the `courtPlots` module unchanged.
   - Expose and Spread clear plots through the existing out-influence check, including the immediate machine check (`src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:742`).
   - If the influence reduction leaves the attacker equal to or above the target, the Scheme stays. Explain that in the reaction.
5. Route `SOCIAL_ACT {act:'rumour', ...}` through the #7 `applySocialAct` transaction.
   - Commit evidence consumption, limits, favour credit, court commands and actor patches once under the existing request ledger.
   - Send the established `APPLY_SOCIAL_RESULT` protocol for influence, response and projections. Apply Hush suspicion through `APPLY_SUSPICION_CHANGE` with request deduplication.
   - Settle all actor mailboxes before evaluating plot defusal or taking a save checkpoint. Plot influence currently comes from actor snapshots (`src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:114`).
   - After influence patches, reconcile derived faction, graph node and membership offers through the existing faction path. Imperial eligibility includes influence ≥0.5 (`src/lib/factionSystem.ts:37`); preserve pledged faction overrides.
   - Preserve the serial rule from #7. Current saves require graph and actor serials to agree (`src/persistence/campaignSave.ts:180`).
   - Actor transitions remain the only source of backing/pledge awards and reports. Rules return results; they never send actor events themselves.
   - Hush prevents a future report. It cannot erase an already committed report, reverse defeat or resurrect a casualty.
6. Extend the existing dialogue and Satchel rumour detail flow.
   - Offer contextual written choices for the selected card, followed by a consequence preview and confirmation. Show exact deltas only in Scholar's View.
   - Threaten, Hush and Expose require two deliberate steps. They never become the initial focus or default Enter target.
   - Keep the suspicion eye and witness names visible. Capture witnesses once when the scene opens; carry that same list through confirmation and receipt.
   - Show a courtier reaction, worded notice and Chronicle entry for success, backfire and a cancelled warning. Update Decrees from committed plot state.
   - Use existing scrolls, lacquer plaques, seal marks, theme tokens and Emblem glyphs. Style additions belong in the theme.
   - Budget 40–60 short authored lines: contextual player choices, outcomes, blocked reasons and Ladies' Court overrides. Follow the #8 voice guide and coverage interface.
   - Extend existing focus, hotkey and reduced-motion handling. Esc backs out of confirmation first, then the card choices, then leaves the scene.
7. Add persistence and simulator coverage in the same PR. Update the glossary and architecture module map for Proof and scheme actions.

## Delete in the same PR

- Replace any #11 placeholder resolver or disabled future-verb rows with the chosen Q2 implementation.
- Remove duplicated card eligibility, consumption and limit checks from React or machine handlers.
- Keep the informational “Ask about” route. Reuse the existing plot resolver, actor protocol, notices and favour book.
- Do not restore deleted gift, insult or romance pipelines, warning banners, native alerts or legacy CSS patches.

## New or changed modules

- `src/lib/courtWhispers.ts`: options, resolution and Proof combination; hides fact matching, limits, spending, backfires and one-warning cancellation.
- `src/lib/applySocialAct.ts`: fold rumour results through the existing transaction; hides graph commands, actor events and checkpoint ordering.
- `src/lib/favours.ts`: bounded favour-owed credit and redemption within its existing seasonal payout budget.
- `src/lib/conversation.ts`, `src/lib/courtView.ts`: typed card choices, confirmation and receipts; UI consumes the view without actor reads.
- `src/data/court/rumourTemplates.ts` and existing voice packs: evidence labels and authored scheme lines.
- `src/state-machines/{game-machine,character-machine}.ts`: routing and the established social-result/suspicion protocol; no new machine states.
- Existing `src/hud/` dialogue, Satchel and Decrees components, plus `src/persistence/campaignSave.ts`: presentation and durable schema.
- `src/lib/courtPlots.ts`: consume its public interface; preserve its implementation and public types.

## Tests

- Extend the #11 whispers interface suite: two distinct sources form Proof; duplicate IDs, stale facts, unrelated subjects and mismatched plot targets fail without spending.
- Table-test every enabled verb, card consumption, directional edges, immunity, caps, patron backfire and rejected actions.
- Hush tests cover fear 0.499/0.5, suspicion floors/ceilings, pledged targets and reports already committed under Q1.
- Test influence crossing 0.5: actor faction, graph node and offers agree after Spread/Expose and restore; pledged overrides stay intact.
- Drive Expose through `resolveCourtSeason`: below target influence defuses; equality stays dangerous; unsuccessful exposure keeps the existing warning and casualty cadence.

No existing public plot API is deleted.

title: S8: Stage the Emperor's herald, tribute, audience and handscroll ending
body:
> Part of #2 · Slice S8 · Size L · Depends on: #4, #6, #7, #8, #9, #10, #11, #12

## What changes for the player

- A herald opens a new career and warns at the Rat watch: “His Majesty may call tonight. Prepare tribute.”
- Concubines see the Night of Slips. Princes receive an imperial summons; scholars see a memorial selected for review.
- Tribute happens in a lantern-lit scene. Present items or pay taels against the same rank demand.
- The final audience uses three authored questions, spoken in the throne hall, with numbered replies.
- Victory and defeat unroll as a handscroll of the career, judgment and recorded court events.

## Why

- Tribute currently makes Refuse the cinnabar primary, beside a payment button: `src/components/EmperorEncounter.tsx:31` and `src/components/EmperorEncounter.tsx:32`.
- The encounter guard applies to every career, starting at season 2: `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:301`. Green-headed slips need career-specific framing.
- `checking_encounters` immediately transitions after drawing RNG: `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:924`. A visible ritual needs an explicit completion boundary.
- The audience leaves the palace view and still sends a browser API key in a request URL: `src/components/GameLayout.tsx:369`, `src/lib/aiServices.ts:314` and `src/lib/aiServices.ts:324`.

## Scope

1. **Settle the lethality contract before implementing consequences.** Record the owner's Q1 answer in #2:
   - A: retain current report and unpaid-tribute execution rules.
   - B: unpaid tribute causes visible demotion or lost access; execution belongs to the final audience.
   - C: unpaid tribute can execute; reports use the softer consequence selected in #11.
   - For B, define the exact tribute penalty, bottom-rank outcome and acknowledgment before coding it. Reuse the career consequence module and notices.
   - Without an answer, preserve existing consequences and keep this decision visibly unresolved. Do not silently adopt recommendation B.
2. **Author the herald and career framing.** Use the selected career title and rank; use “you” where a personal name is unavailable.
   - Never name the player Concubine Mei; that courtier already exists at `src/data/characters.ts:123`.
   - Cold open runs only after a new-campaign action, through local presentation state; loading a save skips it.
   - Warn once on entering Rat in an eligible season. Do not draw the encounter early or promise a summons.
   - Concubine: lacquer tray, green-headed slips, Chief Eunuch's line, selected slip, seal and gong.
   - Prince: herald opens a sealed summons addressed to the player's rank.
   - Scholar: a eunuch announces whether the player's memorial was called for imperial review.
   - Author selected / passed-over / no suitable rival lines for each career. Budget at least 12 opening, warning and ritual lines.
3. **Give the ritual a machine boundary.** Keep the existing `checking_encounters` state; replace its immediate routing with `ACK_EMPEROR_RITUAL` carrying the current season.
   - Draw once on entry exactly as today; derive the selected/passed-over presentation from that stored RNG value and the existing guard.
   - A valid acknowledgment routes through the existing encounter guard to `emperor_encounter` or `advancing_season`.
   - Ignore stale acknowledgments, repeated retirement and payment events during the ritual. Skip and animation completion send the same acknowledgment.
   - Keep the season uncommitted until this boundary completes. Duplicate acknowledgment never pays allowance or advances twice.
   - Choose any shown rival from living, active, career-appropriate courtiers using cosmetic selection. With no candidate, use an unnamed court announcement.
   - A rival reveal emits one presentation notice; it introduces no new hate, support or encounter roll.
4. **Stage imperial scenes through the existing presentation modules.** Map ritual and tribute to `worldMode: cutscene`; map the audience to a locked dialogue scene.
   - Keep the palace mounted during the audience. Replace the early full-screen return with a view selected by `CourtView`.
   - Extend `stageShot` with establishing and imperial beats. Use the existing portrait light, medium framing, gold nameplate and 11vh letterbox.
   - Pause the season clock and movement; retain camera/animation stepping needed for the scene. Block world interaction and pose autosave during shots.
   - Reuse #10's first-visit and rare-event procession policy. A routine Rat warning must not start another procession.
   - Loading failure offers Retry and a software-rendered imperial scene. Payment stays locked until the scene is ready.
   - Provide visible Continue/Skip, reduced-motion cuts and a readable static subtitle. Skip changes presentation duration only.
5. **Resolve tribute by worth through one pure transaction.** Reuse catalogue worth, satchel operations and `tributeCost`; demand remains 10 / 20 / 40 (`src/lib/campaignBalance.ts:19`).
   - The ledger shows purse, required worth and selected offering worth. Item selection supports quantities and combinations, including two worth-20 items for demand 40.
   - Accept either an item bundle whose worth meets the demand, or the full demand in taels. Do not add mixed item-and-tael payment in this slice.
   - Consume exactly the selected bundle; excess worth has no refund or extra favor. Tael payment deducts exactly the demand.
   - Derive preview, affordability, pardon and commit from the same live campaign inventory. Reject missing items, excessive quantities, stale or forged offers with a notice and no debit.
   - Use one typed tribute command with encounter identity and payment data; replace the client-supplied `giftsRemaining` payload.
   - A successful payment consumes one existing favor draw, retaining the 30% chance, influence reward and scaling. Repeated submission has no effect.
   - Pardon requires perceived loyalty **strictly greater than 0.8**, insufficient taels, and insufficient total eligible satchel worth for any valid bundle.
   - Holding an affordable bundle prevents pardon even with an empty purse. Keep Talk's reputation limits from #7; pleading creates no loyalty or support.
   - Plead is available only when that rule grants pardon. It emits a notice and resumes settlement without payment or a favor draw.
   - “Present tribute” is the single primary and default safe action. Refuse is secondary and opens a second step naming the exact consequence.
   - The confirmation defaults to “Return to tribute”. Refuse receives no number shortcut and never becomes the implicit Enter target.
   - Esc cancels refusal confirmation first; it never refuses or leaves an unresolved summons. A long keypress cannot open and confirm refusal.
6. **Replace AI generation and judgment with authored audience rules.** Coordinate with #20; remove the path here if that fix has not landed.
   - `audienceQuestions.ts` owns exactly three questions with three replies for each path: traditional, shadow-ruler, revolutionary and survivor.
   - Author 12 questions and 36 replies in the court voice. Keep survivor content for existing saves; do not add a new eligibility trigger.
   - Reuse faction eligibility and consolidation in `src/lib/emperorAudience.ts:49`. Normalize the scholar's legacy `minister` identity at the existing edge.
   - Move the offline score and context weighting into the audience rules module. Preserve current thresholds and bonus cap unless Q1 explicitly changes them (`src/lib/aiServices.ts:438`).
   - Initialize the child directly at `asking_questions`. Judge synchronously after three valid replies; remove async loading and timeout branches.
   - Keep answer keys a/b/c in stored questions. Display 1/2/3 and route them through the shared scene hotkey handler; reject invalid answers and key repeats.
   - Use a per-question identity to reject stale duplicate submissions. Never let a held key answer the next question.
   - Emit one final result to the parent. Victory/execution end the campaign; failure shows judgment, then the existing demotion acknowledgment and probation.
7. **Replace ending layouts with one handscroll.** Build ordered panels from career, final outcome, Emperor's words and available notices.
   - Notices are bounded; describe retained events honestly. Include a final summary even when the notice list is empty.
   - Preserve career-specific defeat reasons and all existing victory paths. Failure at the audience returns to play instead of displaying a final ending.
   - Use silk, rods, seals, theme typography and tokens. Horizontal scrolling must also work by touch and keyboard; use readable stacked panels on narrow screens.
   - Restart uses the existing new-campaign/save controls. Remove `window.location.reload()` from the audience.
8. **Update the architecture documents.** Describe the audience and tribute owners, add `src/hud/` if earlier slices have not, remove completed AudienceOracle roadmap item 9, and replace the Gemini Known hazards entry with the resolved state. Update Tribute and Audience in the glossary.

## Delete in the same PR

- Old EmperorEncounter CourtDialog wiring and its 2D recovery button; replace its contents with the shared DialogueScene tribute view.
- EmperorAudienceScreen's background-image layout, A/B/C window listener and reload button; replace with the throne-hall scene.
- GameOverScreen's boxed stats layout; replace with the handscroll presentation.
- `aiServices.ts`, Gemini prompts/config/parsers, AI-only input/output types, async audience actors and their 30-second timers after callers move.
- `fallbackQuestions.ts` after authored banks replace it; rename `AIQuestion` to the domain question type without changing its saved shape.
- Duplicate parent audience completion routes; keep one child completion mechanism and one application of its result.
- Obsolete `.audience-screen`, `.ending-screen`, scroll, ledger and related media rules. Move replacement styles into the existing theme; do not patch legacy CSS.
- Obsolete gold-only payment / primary Refuse markup and the taels-only pardon helper, once their transaction replacement owns the behavior.

## New or changed modules

- `src/lib/imperialTribute.ts`: `tributeOptions(campaign)` and `resolveTribute(campaign, request, favorDraw)`; hides worth, stock validation, affordability, pardon and receipts. RNG is supplied at the machine edge.
- `src/lib/emperorAudience.ts`: authored question selection and pure judgment alongside existing path eligibility; hides scoring and career normalization.
- `src/data/court/audienceQuestions.ts`: four complete question banks and authored judgment lines; owns content, with no remote adapter.
- `src/hud/SlipsRitual.tsx`, shared `DialogueScene`, and the handscroll presentation: typed view plus callbacks; hide ritual beats, confirmation and accessible rendering.
- `worldMode`, `courtView`, `dialogueStage`, the two machines and persistence: route those interfaces; keep rules out of React and notices out of rule side effects.

## Tests

- Rewrite `tests/tributeRanks.test.ts` through the tribute transaction, rendered scene and real machine: all career/rank pairs, bundle 40, exact tael debit, invalid stock, overpayment, pardon at 0.8 / above 0.8, owned affordable items, one favor draw and duplicate commit.
- Add ritual renders for all three careers and selected/passed-over/no-rival cases; machine tests for acknowledgment, skip, stale acknowledgment, locked clock and exactly one settlement.
- Add scene interaction tests for 1/2/3 answers, held/stale keys, default tribute focus, two-step refusal, Esc precedence, loading retry and focus return.
- Add audience interface tests for all four banks, score boundaries, capped context bonus, one completion and failure returning to play. Stub network access to throw while driving a real audience through all replies.
- Add handscroll renders for every ending path, career defeat, empty/truncated notices and narrow/reduced-motion states. Test displayed event order through component output.
- Update `tests/gameMachine.test.ts` and `tests/campaignSave.test.ts`: remove injected generation/judgment actors and fallback imports; drive authored answers and resumed stored questions instead.
- Replace old `GIVE_EMPEROR_GIFT` and immediate season-routing assumptions in `tests/campaignRandom.test.ts`, `tests/emperorIntro.test.ts`, `tests/introPendingPlot.test.ts`, `tests/assassinationLifecycle.test.ts`, `tests/hateRules.test.ts` and `tests/playtestMode.test.ts` with ritual acknowledgment plus typed payment; retain their original behavior assertions.
- Update season helpers in `tests/palaceSchedules.test.ts`, `tests/romanceLifecycle.test.ts`, `tests/romancePlots.test.ts`, `tests/rankGiftIncome.test.ts`, and surviving/replacement suites for `tests/seasonalAllyGifts.test.ts`, `tests/demotionNotice.test.ts` and `tests/giftTransactions.test.ts`. Earlier slices may already have replaced those files; update their interface replacements.
- Retain `tests/emperorEntrance.test.ts` for loaded, failed and software-model lifecycle behavior; extend coverage for the shared imperial scene.
- Any surviving `tests/courtIntrigueUI.test.ts` source assertions affected by GameLayout changes become rendered view tests. Add no source/CSS regex tests.
- Update `scripts/simulate-campaign.ts` to acknowledge rituals and choose valid tribute offerings. Compare every policy against the preceding slice, including omniscient, learner and explorer. Include item-tribute economics in the agreed promotion/win-rate gate; preserve career targets.

## Save impact

- No schema bump for presentation alone. Reuse the schema and satchel introduced by dependencies; do not persist shots, ritual progress, confirmation or cold-open state.
- Keep `checking_encounters` outside the checkpoint whitelist. Saving during the ritual retains the last valid checkpoint; loading replays its deterministic draw and never consumes an extra one.
- Preserve `emperor_encounter` and child `asking_questions` checkpoints (`src/persistence/campaignSave.ts:94`, `src/persistence/campaignSave.ts:132`).
- Resuming an audience keeps its saved question text, keys, answers and index; do not replace partly answered questions with the new bank.
- Round-trip v7 golden saves through current migrations and the dependency schema at pending tribute and after each saved question. Verify inventory, RNG and pending season settlement survive.
- If Q1 requires additional persisted consequence state, ship the next unused schema version, migration, validators and round trips together. Coordinate with #15 rather than assuming its planned v11 is still available.

## Review notes to handle

- Must fix 5: pardon checks taels and every payable item bundle; free Talk cannot farm loyalty. Must fix 14: safe primary, explicit refusal confirmation and no lethal default hotkey.
- Should fix career fiction, duplicate player name, tribute 40, audience content budget, input collisions and typewriter accessibility are requirements above.
- Use a full-line live region and mark animated character spans `aria-hidden`; do not read one letter at a time. Skip/reduced motion preserve the complete subtitle.
- Keep cosmetic draws independent of campaign RNG; preserve encounter and favor order. Measure the item economy in the S8 sim gate.
- Resolve #20 completely. With one authored implementation, delete the AudienceOracle proposal rather than adding a one-adapter port.

## Hooks that need the owner's OK

- None expected with the existing frame loop, `useReducer`, scene hotkey routing, ref callbacks and `onAnimationEnd` for ritual completion. Provide explicit Continue so missing animation events cannot stall the campaign.
- Lazy Emperor loading/disposal, ritual timers and focus return are the pressure points. Reuse palace model leases, frame stepping and focus refs; do not add `useEffect`, `useMemo`, `useCallback` or a subscription for them silently.
- If those alternatives cannot satisfy lifecycle behavior, ask the owner about the exact proposed effect/subscription before implementation. State its cleanup and why the frame/ref alternative fails. Remove the existing audience listener effect.

## How to check it

1. Start each career. Read the herald title; reload a save and confirm the cold open does not replay.
2. Set a five-minute season in Settings. Reach Rat after season 1, read the warning, then Retire. Compare slips, summons and memorial framing.
3. Use pending-tribute QA saves at demands 10 / 20 / 40. Pay with taels, one item and a bundle. Check the receipt and one season advance.
4. Try Refuse, press Esc, then reopen it. Read the consequence. Verify Enter/held keys never confirm it accidentally. Exercise pardon with and without affordable items.
5. Load an audience checkpoint for each path. Answer by mouse and 1/2/3; reload midway and finish with network disabled. Verify judgment and demotion/ending.
6. Read the handscroll on desktop and phone-sized viewports, with reduced motion. Test Retry/software recovery, keyboard focus and the new-campaign control.

## Done when

- `npm run check` and `npm run build` pass.
- You loaded the game and looked at the change on desktop and a phone-sized viewport.
- Tribute, save/reload, refusal, all career framings and all audience outcomes meet the interface tests and agreed simulator gate.
- Q1's applied consequences are recorded; #20 is resolved and no audience request uses a network service.
