title: S7: Favours and palace discoveries with a shared seasonal reward budget
body:
> Part of #2 · Slice S7 · Size L · Depends on: #11 (and its #7, #8, #9, #10 prerequisites)

## What changes for the player

- Present courtiers occasionally ask for lotus seeds, a sealed-letter delivery, or something you have heard.
- Lotus, plum blossom, tea and old scrolls glint at reachable places around the palace.
- Lost belongings have clues to their owners. You can return them or keep a modest gift.
- Hidden whisper slips reveal palace lore and fill each compound's exploration percentage.
- Helping someone reveals tastes and can strengthen their backing. Promotion still follows global support and influence.
- One chosen favour can have a map pin. The decree tracker keeps its focus on career progress and danger.

## Why

- The first-rank Concubine allowance is 20; extra free items and support can overwhelm that pacing (`src/lib/campaignBalance.ts:18`).
- Proper already has a defined support value: +9 for Concubine, +10 for Prince and Scholar before scaling (`src/lib/campaignBalance.ts:28`). Use that ceiling for favours.
- The graph already accepts support commands with `formPledge` (`src/lib/courtGraph.ts:54`). Actors issue milestone rewards (`src/state-machines/character-machine.ts:97`); paying those rewards inside favours would duplicate them.
- Five playable zones already exist (`src/palace/zones.ts:12`). Discoveries should make their props and routes useful without changing career access.

## Scope

1. **Extend the shared supply economy first.**
   - `palaceSupply` owns one free-value budget per campaign season across all zones and all S7 rewards.
   - Start with a named, tunable cap of 10 taels of equivalent value. Tune it against the simulation gate below.
   - Charge gathered items, kept belongings and item rewards at catalogue worth, including their sell-back value.
   - Price support rewards as the equivalent fraction of a Proper present to that recipient, using the existing tier-worth table.
   - Reserve rewards when generating an opportunity. A reward cannot exceed its reservation or change after acceptance.
   - Treat knowledge-only rewards as zero value. Any support or item bundled with a reveal must still be charged.
   - Keep spent and reserved value in campaign state. Failed actions spend nothing; reopening a room never refills it.
   - Reset the budget exactly once at committed season rollover. Promotion, watch changes and load do not reset it.

2. **Add optional favours through conversation.**
   - Deterministically offer up to 2–3 per season from living, present givers in accessible zones; fewer is valid.
   - Support bring-item/tag, sealed-letter delivery and sharing an already-known rumour.
   - Check that the destination is accessible and the schedule leaves a chance to complete the favour before expiry.
   - Keep at most one accepted favour per courtier. Declining or ignoring an offer has no penalty.
   - Show the request, promised reward and season-end expiry before Accept. Carry letters as favour facts, outside the gift satchel.
   - Require an explicit handover to the correct present recipient. Gathering alone records progress without completing it.
   - Consume requested items atomically with completion. Sharing a rumour requires the actual known card or fact.
   - Calculate support through the existing Proper scaling and rounding path; cap the reward at Proper before scaling.
   - Mood, signature tastes and court tier cannot upgrade a favour to Pleasing or Treasured.
   - Pay positive favour support once per courtier per season. Share this limit with lost-item return support.
   - Emit a giver-to-player support command with `formPledge: true`; use #7's `applySocialAct` and actor-result protocol.
   - A letter also emits its authored directed giver-to-recipient support command. Reserve that reward too; never create an NPC pledge from delivery.
   - Record the promised, truthful taste reveal through Brush Notes with its favour source, season and watch.
   - Expire accepted unfinished favours once at season end: -4 giver-to-player support, no hate. Unaccepted offers expire silently.
   - Cancel without penalty when a required courtier dies or is permanently expelled. Ordinary watch departures preserve progress.

3. **Add gathering and lost belongings to world interactions.**
   - Author 4–6 candidate grade-1 gather spots in each entry zone; activate only what the shared budget can fund.
   - Gather once per spot per season. Reject unknown, distant, obstructed, inaccessible or already-gathered spots.
   - Author up to 1–2 lost-item opportunities per zone per season, subject to the same campaign-wide budget.
   - Give each instance a stable season/zone/id, one real owner and a caption grounded in that owner's authored taste or office.
   - Keep found belongings in the discovery state until Return or Keep settles the instance; they cannot also be gifted or sold.
   - Kept items are grade 1 or 2 only. Choose this bounded option from the red-team review; omit the theft-risk branch in S7.
   - Returning to the correct present owner grants the reserved warmth and sourced taste reveal once. Wrong-owner attempts change nothing.
   - A kept instance can never later pay a return reward. A returned instance can never grant an item.
   - A full satchel leaves the spot or instance available and spends no budget or collection flag.

4. **Add persistent whisper slips and knowledge perks.**
   - Ship eight authored slips in each of the five playable zones: 40 stable ids and lore lines.
   - Place them at reachable lattices, eaves and bookcases. A nearby ear glyph and chime hint at them within 20 m.
   - Compute zone progress from unique collected ids / the zone's authored total. Slips remain collected across seasons.
   - At 50%, widen that zone's Listen range by 2 m once. Keep witness and detection geometry unchanged.
   - At 100%, grant one truthful Brush Notes reveal once. Persist the reveal and its source.
   - Lore is authored; any live rumour or taste claim must resolve against campaign facts through #11's knowledge path.
   - Slips grant knowledge only. They never add taels, support, influence, inventory or discounts.

5. **Integrate presentation through the existing world and HUD.**
   - Extend `WORLD_ACT` with gather, lost-item pickup/keep/return and slip collection; extend `SOCIAL_ACT favour` with accept/hand-in.
   - Use typed ids, `requestId`, season/watch and the existing action-time access/presence checks. Ignore client-supplied reward amounts.
   - Persist semantic collection/completion ids as well as the processed-request ledger: changing the request id cannot repeat a reward.
   - Route all mutations synchronously through the existing campaign command reducer and actor projections. Add no machine states.
   - Put glints and simple procedural props in `worldProps`; use the existing interaction stack, minimap and waypoint.
   - Offer Track explicitly. Show only the selected favour's destination pin; keep details with its giver in People/Brush Notes.
   - Do not add a favour board, a task tab, repeated `FAVOUR` tracker lines or automatic tracking of every request.
   - Use lacquer prompts, silk detail panes, `Emblem`, theme tokens and `playCue`. Respect sound settings and reduced motion.
   - Show a visible discovery cue as well as sound. Keep prompts above touch controls and operable with keyboard and tap.
   - Derive stock, favours and lost-item picks from `campaignStream(campaignSeed, season, purpose)`; never advance `rngState`.
   - Content budget: 10 reusable favour scripts covering all three kinds and career entry zones, including Maid He's lotus request; five lost-item caption/return sets; 40 slips; contextual player replies.
   - Allow roughly 120–150 authored lines, including offer/accept/reminder/completion/expiry text. Remaining personal scripts belong to #16.
   - Maid He is an example when present. Use a deterministic fixture for her browser check; ordinary campaigns retain their real cast.

6. **Ship the v10 migration and paired balance gate in the same slice.**
   - Follow the save and simulation requirements below before merging the visible feature.

## Delete in the same PR

- No existing gameplay module needs deletion solely for S7.
- Replace #7's reserved gathering stub and any temporary discovery lists with the shared `palaceSupply` implementation.
- Replace duplicate collection/reward checks in world, HUD or machine handlers with the public rules interfaces.
- Remove any prerequisite favour tracker placeholders when adding explicit Track. Retain decree and scheme priorities.
- Keep styles in the established theme; delete any displaced legacy rules rather than adding overrides to frozen CSS.

## New or changed modules

- `src/lib/favours.ts`: `offerFavours(input)`, `noteWorldFact(book, fact)`, `resolveFavour(input, act)`, `expire(book, season)`. Owns eligibility, progress, expiry and graph/fact commands; returns updated slices and results.
- `src/lib/palaceSupply.ts`: extend the public supply operations for gathering, lost-item settlement and slip collection. Hides reservations, shared valuation, unique claims, respawn and exploration rewards.
- `src/data/court/{favours,gatherSpots,lostItems,slips}.ts`: stable, typed content ids, reachable anchors, truthful owner clues and complete scripts.
- `src/palace/worldProps.ts`: create/sync/step/dispose discovery props. Owns glints, visibility, software-renderer substitutes and resource cleanup; rules receive action facts as arguments.
- Extend `applySocialAct`, `conversation`, `courtView`, `interactables`, `earshot`, `PalaceMenu`, the minimap and `game-machine` through their existing interfaces. Keep reward arithmetic inside rules modules.
- Extend `src/persistence/campaignSave.ts`; document favours, discovery state and module ownership in `docs/GLOSSARY.md` and `docs/architecture/README.md`.

## Tests

- Add `tests/favours.test.ts`: deterministic eligible offers; inaccessible/dead targets excluded; decline; item/tag hand-in; known-rumour requirement; correct letter direction; duplicate completion; one seasonal support payment; expiry once with no hate.
- Extend `tests/palaceSupply.test.ts` from #7: mixed gather/keep/return/favour rewards never exceed the shared cap; reservations; grade caps; cross-zone and watch reloads; full satchel; reset once; fresh request ids cannot bypass claims.
- Add lost-item cases through that interface: wrong owner changes nothing; Return and Keep are mutually exclusive; correct owner and reward survive restore.
- Add slip cases through that interface: unique percentage, 50%/100% grants once, persistent collection, factual reveal and no economic rewards.

title: S6: Whispers and witnesses in the living court
body:
> Part of #2 · Slice S6 · Size L · Depends on: #7, #8, #9, #10

## What changes for the player

- Live gossip spots carry a brush-stroke ripple. Hide nearby and Listen for four seconds to learn a rumour.
- Rumour cards reveal real tastes, factions, grudges, lovers, suspicion and pending plots.
- Conversations show the named witnesses captured when the scene opened. A present in an empty chamber has no spectators.
- Being caught listening brings a spoken reaction and a visible suspicion warning.
- The Satchel holds rumour cards. A conversation can offer a contextual “Ask about…” reply.
- Plot rumours name the attacker one watch before the public Scheme warning.

## Why

- Gift witnesses currently come from every name present in the zone: `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:812`. Distance and screens have no effect.
- Romance does the same: `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:787`. Its lifecycle test counts the recipient as a witness: `tests/romanceLifecycle.test.ts:192`.
- One report currently ends a concubine campaign: `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:615`. Adding detection needs an explicit lethality decision.
- Plot warnings currently appear as a pinned button: `src/components/GameLayout.tsx:401`. The plot engine already supplies real attackers and deadlines: `src/lib/courtPlots.ts:102`.

## Scope

1. **Resolve Q1 before this lands.** Record the owner's choice on #2 and link it in the PR:
   - A: retain report defeats and unpaid-tribute execution, with explicit warnings.
   - B: reports build visible pressure leading to demotion or lost access; execution belongs to the Emperor's audience.
   - C: soften reports into pressure; retain tribute execution at the Night of Slips.
   - B is the plan's recommendation. It has no recorded approval in this brief.
   - If B or C wins, specify thresholds, consequences and migration defaults in a linked prerequisite. Land that rule change before enabling Listen detection. Coordinate tribute presentation with #13.
2. **Implement one witness rule: capture at scene opening.** Replace the plan's action-time sampling:
   - Capture living named spectators in the current zone, within 8 m horizontally of the player's interaction anchor, with unobstructed head-to-head sight.
   - Exclude the player, conversation partner, deceased courtiers and ambient extras. Keep target-presence guards separate.
   - Use the world collider/view-blocker bounds. Return unique names in stable order. NPC facing does not restrict ordinary witnesses.
   - Put the captured names, zone and watch on transient conversation state. Use that same list for every preview and `SOCIAL_ACT` in the scene.
   - Other courtiers may stroll. Later arrivals never enter this list; departures never trigger a re-sample. Label the row “Witnesses when you began”.
   - Leaving and reopening captures a fresh list. Zone/watch changes or a dead participant invalidate the scene and require reopening.
3. **Make witness effects consume that list.** Extend the #7 social resolver and its existing actor protocol:
   - Resolve witness traits from campaign data; geometry stays at the palace boundary.
   - Rebel risk follows whichever tag produced the ambitious fit, including martial/ambitious items. A `seditious`-only check would leave an escape route.
   - Preserve eligible Imperial/Loyalist witness risk +0.10 and the hostile multiplier ×1.5; tradition relief remains -0.05 for eligible witnesses.
   - Concubine intimate acts/proposals apply +0.10 to eligible unpledged spectators. End-romance remains exempt.
   - The partner retains recipient effects, but gains no extra suspicion merely by being counted as their own spectator.
   - Use one typed witness fact shape. Replace actor-reading loyal-benefit calculations with pure inputs; the current entry is `src/lib/crossCharacterEffects.ts:131`.
4. **Add Listen to authored gossip spots from #10.** Offer it through #9 interactables only when two or more living scheduled speakers occupy the group:
   - Within an 8 m listening radius, accumulate four continuous seconds while hidden from every speaker.
   - Detection uses each speaker's full 70-degree view cone, an 8 m range and unobstructed sight. A screen or bookcase blocks detection.
   - Leaving range, losing the group or being detected resets progress. Menus, scenes, hidden tabs and frozen world frames add no progress.
   - On detection, emit one caught outcome per spot/watch. Each detecting speaker gains +0.05 suspicion once through the existing reporting protocol.
   - Show the detecting names and risk before starting. Warn explicitly if that increment reaches a report threshold under the selected Q1 rules.
   - `WORLD_ACT listen` carries requestId, spotId, season, watch and the observed group/outcome. Validate the spot and scheduled group, dedupe requests, and consume the spot/watch attempt on success or detection.
5. **Build rumours from facts.** `courtWhispers` owns selection, cards and Listen results:
   - Candidate kinds: authored taste, undiscovered faction, directed hate ≥30, mutual romance, suspicion within 0.10 of a report threshold, and a real pending plot.
   - Inject graph, tastes, suspicion facts, plots, knowledge and the #7 `campaignStream(campaignSeed, season, 'whispers')` stream. Never consume `rngState`.
   - Bind every card to a typed fact and source: speakers, zone, spot, season and watch. No fabricated edges, factions or prospective deaths.
   - Check the fact again on completion. If no fact remains, show a short flavour line and grant no card.
   - Deduplicate by fact identity. Keep at most 20 cards; evict the oldest non-active-plot card first. Active safety warnings also live in Decrees/Chronicle.
   - Preserve historical cards as dated testimony; revalidate actionable questions and mark changed facts stale.
   - “Ask about…” reveals or discusses existing information. It grants no support, reputation or plot cancellation. Confide, Spread, Threaten, Hush, Expose and proof mechanics belong to #14.
6. **Define “one watch early” without inventing future plots.** During the first watch after a pending plot is committed, its fact is available to Listen. Publish its Scheme entry and notice at the next watch boundary:
   - Keep `warnedSeason`, `dueSeason`, defusing, shields and casualties unchanged. The engine grants a full season before the first attempt: `src/lib/courtPlots.ts:102`.
   - Warn automatically even if the player never Listens, the attacker is elsewhere or the card bound is full.
   - On early retirement/Next season, present any unpublished warning before committing the boundary. Reload must preserve this obligation.
   - Existing migrated pending plots get an immediate public warning. Cancelled plots cease to yield current warnings.
7. **Present the experience and ship v9 together.** Extend the existing DialogueScene, Satchel tab, Scheme tracker and notice flow:
   - Use theme tokens, silk rumour slips, an ear Emblem and a seal on acquisition. Add the glyph through `src/ui`; use `playCue('scroll')` once.
   - Keep text at least 13px. Use a clear keyboard/touch Listen action, visible cancel and status text alongside the progress ring.
   - The full whisper goes in a single accessible live node; animated character spans are aria-hidden. Reduced motion shows the line immediately.
   - Budget roughly 40 authored lines: at least 18 fact templates across the six kinds, plus caught reactions and contextual questions. Reuse #8 voices; validate every applicable template binding.

## Delete in the same PR

- Zone-wide witness construction at `src/components/GameLayout.tsx:319` and the equivalent gift/romance handler paths, or their surviving #7 replacements.
- Actor-reading loyal-benefit plumbing replaced by typed campaign facts. Delete superseded tests with that implementation.
- The pinned intrigue-banner path and its legacy CSS if #9 has not already removed them. Keep one Scheme warning route.
- Duplicate witness types, geometry checks or rumour state created during the prerequisite slices. Extend their owning modules.

## New or changed modules

- `src/palace/earshot.ts`: `witnessesAt(input) → names`; `listenState(input) → {eligible, detectedBy}`. Owns radius, cones and occlusion over numeric poses/blockers, with no three.js dependency.
- `src/lib/courtWhispers.ts`: `whispersFor(input)`, `overhear(book, observation)`, `rumourOptions(scene)`. Owns factual selection, source records, attempt limits, card bounds and stale knowledge.
- `src/data/court/rumourTemplates.ts`: typed authored templates; owns wording and required fact fields.
- Existing conversation/social modules: own the frozen scene list and its receipt; `giftTransaction`, `courtIntrigue`, `courtRomance` and `crossCharacterEffects` consume it.
- Existing palace director/frame loop: supplies current positions, group membership and facing. `PalaceScene` already has blockers and a sight test at `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:129`.
- Existing `courtView`, objectives, HUD and persistence: expose knowledge and due warnings; keep rule selection out of React and the machine.

## Tests

- Add `earshot.test.ts`: exact 8 m boundary, wall/screen occlusion, 35-degree cone half-angle, rear approach, all-speaker detection, empty room, duplicate/dead/off-zone exclusion. Use numeric fixtures and `createPalaceWorld` blocker fixtures.
- Add `courtWhispers.test.ts`: each card has a true source fact; thresholds and directed edges; deterministic selection without `Math.random`; no `rngState` advance; stale facts; 20-card bound; same-watch success/caught replay; next-watch eligibility.
- Extend the conversation and gift-transaction interface suites introduced by #4/#7: preview = receipt while an NPC crosses the radius or blocker after opening; close/reopen refreshes witnesses.
- Change `tests/gameMachine.test.ts` witness cases to explicit spatially selected lists; replace its old message-based helper call at line 31 with the current social interface. Cover loyal relief, Rebel tag risk, idempotency and reports paid once.
- Change `tests/romanceLifecycle.test.ts`: replace recipient-as-witness assertions and zone-wide spectator fixtures with explicit lists. Preserve affection, refusal, pledge immunity and End exemption; assert the selected Q1 report outcome.
- Change `tests/courtRomance.test.ts` witness cases to the shared input shape; retain exact threshold rounding and career exemptions.
- Extend `tests/campaignSave.test.ts` and `tests/campaignSaveMigration.test.ts` for v9 defaults, invalid cards/ledgers and reload deduplication. Retain `tests/romanceSaveValidation.test.ts` projection coverage.
- Extend #9 HUD/menu render suites for named witnesses, rumour source/date, stale questions, empty Satchel and automatic warnings. `tests/romanceUI.test.ts` and `tests/courtIntrigueUI.test.ts` source checks should already be replaced by #3–#9; do not restore them.
- Preserve `tests/courtPlots.test.ts`, `tests/romancePlots.test.ts`, `tests/assassinationLifecycle.test.ts`, `tests/introPendingPlot.test.ts` and `tests/playtestMode.test.ts` cadence/casualty coverage. Add public-warning timing tests through the campaign interface.
- Update `scripts/simulate-campaign.ts` to supply deterministic spatial observations and explicit lists, including private and crowded acts. Compare all policy medians to #7; use its omniscient comparison and owner-approved learner band. Report deaths/reports by cause. Tune witness exposure before changing career targets.

## Save impact

- Bump v8 to v9. Current checkout is v7: `src/persistence/campaignSave.ts:16`; #7 supplies v8 first.
- Persist the bounded rumour book, current-watch Listen attempt ledger and plot-warning publication ledger. Conversation positions, progress and witness snapshots remain transient.
- Migrate v8 to empty knowledge/attempts. Mark existing pending plots for immediate public warning; consume no RNG and preserve relationships, support, suspicion and plot deadlines.
- Validate card kinds, catalogue/graph identifiers, finite thresholds, text lengths, unique IDs, source season/watch, spot IDs, ledger bounds and pending-plot references. Historical deceased speakers remain valid source names.
- Ship a golden v8-to-v9 parse/capture/reload/advance-one-season round trip. Reload cannot grant the same card or caught penalty again, or hide an unpublished warning.
- If Q1 adds pressure state, its approved prerequisite must provide deterministic defaults and validators; no implicit rule conversion in this migration.

## Review notes to handle

- **Must fix 10:** scene-opening capture is the chosen rule. Moving NPCs cannot change a committed preview. Test entry, departure and reopening.
- **Must fix 8:** risk follows the ambitious-fit tag, preserving the #7 fix for martial gifts.
- **Must fix 3 / sim should-fix:** gate the learner using visible witness names, verdicts and Brush Notes; an omniscient-only pass cannot approve this slice. Keep the existing Scholar's View default until the learner gate passes.
- **Lethality Q1:** blocked from landing until the owner answers and required rule changes are implemented. Never quietly assume option A.
- **Should-fix content/accessibility/hook pressure:** include the line budget, accessible full subtitle and hook-free frame-loop plan above in review.

## Hooks that need the owner's OK

- None expected. Use the existing palace frame loop for progress/detection and its telemetry callback for HUD state; do not add timer effects or subscriptions. The current loop is at `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:436`.
- Use existing scene state and ref callbacks for focus. Use one action callback for acquisition sound. Reuse #4 worldMode/visibility handling.
- If implementation requires a new useEffect/useMemo/useCallback or subscription, list its exact purpose for owner approval first. The alternative is the existing director step plus callback boundary.

## How to check it

1. In a known dusk gossip fixture, approach the Ladies' Court garden screens. Confirm the ripple appears only with two scheduled speakers.
2. Hide behind a screen, choose Listen and wait four seconds. Read the whisper, then open Satchel and inspect its named sources and date.
3. Step into a speaker's view during another attempt. Confirm one caught reaction, the named suspicion change and the Q1-approved consequence. Retry that spot in the same watch; no second penalty or card.
4. Open a conversation in an empty chamber, then beside the gossip group. Compare the captured witness rows and receipts. Let a spectator stroll across the boundary; the open scene's list stays fixed.
5. Reload after acquiring a card. The card and consumed attempt remain; half-finished progress resets. Ask about the rumour without earning free support.
6. Use a pending-plot fixture. Overhear its attacker during the early watch, then see the automatic Scheme warning next watch. Repeat without Listening and with early retirement; the warning still arrives before an attempt.
7. Check phone controls, keyboard focus, sound mute and reduced motion. Verify no generic box panels, emoji or unreadable type appear.

## Done when

- Q1 is recorded and its required rule changes have landed.
- Frozen witness previews match receipts; Listen grants only factual, bounded knowledge.
- v8/v9 migration and the automatic warning deadline survive reload and early retirement.
- The all-policy sim gate passes with reports/deaths explained.
- `npm run check` and `npm run build` pass.
- You loaded the game and looked at the change.
- Code review done with GPT-6.1 Sol via T3 delegate_task (owner's rule).

title: S5: Give the court named watches, daily routines and a rare imperial procession
body:
> Part of #2 · Slice S5 · Size L · Depends on: #5, #7, #8, #9

## What changes for the player

- Four named watches mark the moon: Dragon, Horse, Rooster and Rat. A drum and ink wash mark each change.
- Courtiers gather for Morning Greeting, meet at tea tables and garden screens, and face their companions.
- Servants carry trays through the palace. Pond life and shrine smoke add quiet movement.
- The first imperial procession waits until a conversation has finished, or four minutes of active roaming have passed.
- Bow earns a ceremonial acknowledgment. Leaving it unanswered carries no penalty.
- The court stays usable on phones, with fewer ambient extras when frame rate falls.

## Why

- Placement and patrol destinations share a grid; courtiers walk at a fixed speed and bob vertically (`src/palace/world.ts:293`, `src/palace/world.ts:306`, `src/palace/world.ts:343`, `src/palace/world.ts:359`).
- A watch roster change rebuilds the renderer and world (`src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:448`). The curtain must cover that change until #15 delivers continuous arrivals.
- The first visit fires at 75 seconds in a machine guard. Its save checkpoint requires that exact elapsed value (`src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:757`, `src/persistence/campaignSave.ts:137`).
- The Emperor is scheduled into the Ladies' Court every season in phase 2 (`src/palace/zones.ts:43`). That schedule alone must never start a procession.

## Scope

1. **Extract the season clock and name its watches.**
   - Replace the inline interval controller in `src/components/GameLayout.tsx:244` with `seasonClock`.
   - Accept elapsed time and #4's `worldMode` result. Return remaining time, watch identity and boundary/expiry events.
   - Preserve the existing 5/10/15/20-minute lengths and saved presentation clock. Derive watch index from progress; emit expiry once.
   - Phase 0: Dragon · Morning Greeting; 1: Horse · Free Hours; 2: Rooster · Dusk Gossip; 3: Rat · Night.
   - Use one `{season, phase}` watch key for the HUD, presence, Talk/present limits and later Listen. A curtain must never reset social limits.
   - Scenes, menus, loading, transitions, cutscenes and hidden tabs pause campaign time. Reject suspension-sized deltas.

2. **Author spots in all five playable zones.**
   - Add 10–16 spots per zone: tea, guqin, pond rail, shrine, aisle, greeting focal, gossip circle and screen hide.
   - Place approach positions beside props, outside their collider footprints. Include facing, capacity and activity metadata.
   - Use the existing room geometry and navigator. Validate both software worlds and worlds with room focals enabled.
   - Reachability covers spawn, each gate, residential passages and all assigned spots. Keep gate lanes clear.
   - Choose two near-entry sightlines when at least two courtiers are present and reachable spots permit it.
   - Use the actual entry/player pose, including side gates and reloads. Entry-distance sorting selects initial positions only.
   - Keep a separate, spatially spread set of activity destinations. Changing entry direction must preserve that spread.

3. **Replace grid patrols with a pure planner and one director.**
   - `planCourtLife` takes present living courtiers, tiers, the court graph, zone, watch, entry pose, spots and campaign seed.
   - Use #8's `cosmeticPick` for deterministic ties. Planning never consumes campaign `rngState`.
   - Morning Greeting selects the highest-tier present courtier as host, then assigns reachable attendant positions around the focal spot.
   - Other watches distribute tea, pond and guqin activities. Dusk groups use strongest directed support ≥38 or hate ≥30 edges.
   - Break ties by stable name order; bound groups by spot capacity. Empty rooms and single-courtier rooms remain valid.
   - Majors hold their stations. The director owns paths, waits, collision avoidance, facing and engaged holds.
   - Match walking speed to each rig's authored gait. Ground height owns vertical placement; remove the sine bob.
   - Hold an engaged partner in place. Observe the scene freeze policy and keep #4's dialogue shots working.
   - Expose named positions for the minimap and #11's spatial witnesses; extras never enter this list.
   - Keep rebuilding on changed rosters in this slice. Reserve continuous `syncRoster` arrival/departure work for #15.
   - Write opening captions generically for the actual host and companions. Preserve the sampled active cast and career access.
   - Content budget: four watch headings, up to eight activity labels and six short generic herald/greeting/Bow lines. Reuse #8 voices.

4. **Cover each watch rebuild before it happens.**
   - Queue the next roster, raise an ink-wash cover, then commit the roster once the cover is opaque.
   - Nominal transition: 1.2 seconds, one drum and the new watch name. Hold the cover until the new world is ready.
   - A same-roster watch still gets the name/drum and new intents. Update dusk/night lighting in place, like `src/palace/world.ts:318`.
   - Loading failures expose recovery under the cover. Avoid a timed reveal of an unfinished world.
   - Reduced motion uses a brief opacity change. Muting silences the drum. Add a synthesized `drum` cue through `src/ui/sound.ts`.
   - Keep season allowance recaps and demotion acknowledgment separate from watch transitions. A watch never acknowledges a demotion.
   - Move touched transition styles into the existing unlayered theme. Use theme tokens, display type and lacquer/ink surfaces.

5. **Retime and restage the first procession, with a save bump.**
   - Keep `emperor_intro` as the existing campaign checkpoint; presentation stages the herald, entrance, Bow window and exit.
   - Persist `firstConversationDone`. Set it only after an accepted Talk result, through #7's social-action path.
   - On the next active-roam tick after scene exit, enter the first visit if this flag is true or accumulated free-roam elapsed ≥240 seconds.
   - Persist the existing done marker and elapsed clock. Set done on entry, so saving during the procession cannot schedule another introduction.
   - Cancel the pending introduction when a regular imperial encounter or audience supersedes it. Preserve existing tribute/encounter rules for #13.
   - Stage the first visit in the player's current accessible zone. Normal Emperor scheduling is a separate presence rule.
   - Play a generic herald line, gong and six-second entrance with ceremony bars; then offer a six-second Bow window in the interaction stack.
   - Bow yields a SealStamp, “His Majesty acknowledges your greeting,” once per appearance. This slice's reward is cosmetic.
   - Skipping Bow changes no support, hate, suspicion, influence, currency or pardon values. Tier-4 greeting Bows use the same cosmetic rule.
   - Ordinary scheduled visits have no forced ceremony. Ship only the first procession here; rare later processions require an explicit happening ID in #16.
   - Lazy-load the Emperor for an actual appearance, with abort, stale-result rejection, retry and resource release. Allow leaving a failed introductory appearance.
   - Use procedural head turns and a clamped spine bend, restoring the original pose afterward. Idle/Walk rigs must work without #17.
   - If #17 supplies emotes, bind by bone name and strip translation plus sleeve/cloth/hair tracks. Preserve existing cast assets and clip locks.

6. **Add ambient extras within one frame budget.**
   - Reuse servant/eunuch archetypes with tray/sweeping props; add inexpensive koi and shrine smoke only where the zone has those features.
   - Extras have renderer-owned IDs. Never add them to `NAMES`, campaign actors, the court graph, saves, Map people or social targeting.
   - Cap animated character rigs at 10 per zone, counting player, Emperor, named courtiers and human extras together.
   - Keep every scheduled courtier present and selectable. Overflow courtiers remain planted; prioritize player, Emperor and engaged/nearby courtiers for animation.
   - Throttle permitted mixers to at most 10 Hz beyond 15 m or offscreen. Disable actor shadows beyond 12 m.
   - Under coarse pointer, disable extras after average FPS stays below 30 for two seconds; re-enable only above 40 for five seconds.
   - Apply budget decisions to the Emperor mixer too. Resume without accumulated-time jumps. Software rendering uses safe gesture no-ops and no extras.
   - Expose budget decisions through the runtime's public diagnostics for acceptance tests; dispose all extra resources on rebuild/unmount.

## Delete in the same PR

- Grid candidates, shared patrol `route.stops`, roaming flags and the NPC movement loop in `world.animate` (`src/palace/world.ts:290`, `src/palace/world.ts:328`).
- Hard-coded “Walking the gallery”/“Waiting for an audience” assignments and vertical bob (`src/palace/world.ts:358`).
- The inline season interval, old 75-second trigger/countdown, and first-visit duration branch in `emperorEntrancePlan`.
- The introductory acknowledgment modal path when the procession replaces it. Keep regular tribute presentation until #13.
- Touched legacy transition CSS and source-regex demotion assertions. Keep season recap behavior behind its new tested interface.

## New or changed modules

| Module | Public interface | Hides |
|---|---|---|
| `src/lib/seasonClock.ts` | `createSeasonClock(saved) → {tick, snapshot, reset}` | Pause rules from worldMode, watch boundaries, expiry dedupe; injected deltas only |
| `src/data/palaceSpots.ts` | Typed spot catalogue keyed by playable zone | Authored approach/facing positions, capacities and activity destinations |
| `src/lib/courtLife.ts` | `planCourtLife(input) → {intents, groups}` | Greeting host, relationship groups, deterministic placement and route spread |
| `src/palace/courtLifeDirector.ts` | `createCourtLifeDirector(world, navigator) → {apply, step, positions, dispose}` | Steering, holds, facing and renderer-owned extras |
| `src/lib/firstEmperorVisit.ts` | `firstVisitDue(state)` and validated free-roam ticks | Persisted eligibility and the four-minute fallback |
| `src/palace/emperorEntrance.ts` | Appearance plan and `step(dt, mode) → phase/actions` | Entrance/Bow deadlines, skip and completion dedupe |
| Existing clock/HUD, `SeasonTransition`, `PalaceScene`, `world`, `characterModels`, machine and persistence | Consume the interfaces above | Thin integration; rendering budgets stay at the palace edge |

Update `docs/GLOSSARY.md` with watch names and cosmetic Bow. Update the architecture map and remove completed clock/presence roadmap work.

## Tests

- Add planner tests for deterministic output, unchanged `rngState`, strongest-edge grouping, tier host, stationary majors, capacities and absent named cast.
- Test entry sightlines and destination spread from south, east and west entries; include zero/one courtier and a full sampled cast.
- Add world/director interface tests for every spot's reachability, dynamic collisions, engaged holds, grounded gait, saved-pose restore and worldFrozen.
- Add fake-delta clock and transition tests: paused/hidden tabs, every length, boundary once, expiry once, cover-before-rebuild, ready-before-reveal and reduced motion.
- Add budget tests with fake visibility/distance/FPS: 10-rig cap, Emperor inclusion, throttle/shadow cutoffs, extras hysteresis and unchanged named presence.
- Add procession tests: committed Talk then scene exit, 240-second fallback, no scheduled-season replay, Bow once, skip without campaign changes, load abort/retry/disposal.
- Existing suites to replace/update in this PR:
  - `tests/palaceSchedules.test.ts`: preserve deterministic zone partitions; replace placement assertions with planner/director reachability.
  - `tests/palaceZones.test.ts`: replace patrol-stop and fixed .65 m/s checks with spot paths, gait bounds, freeze and saved-pose behavior.
  - `tests/ladiesResidences.test.ts`: replace route-stop checks with reachable residential spots; preserve chamber geometry/restore checks.
  - `tests/palaceRoomFocals.test.ts`: replace route-stop checks through director output; retain physical floors, gates and disposal.
  - `tests/emperorEntrance.test.ts`: replace intro-duration/modal assertions with procession/Bow rendering; retain regular tribute loading locks and asset-pool tests.
  - `tests/emperorIntro.test.ts`: replace 75-second/equality cases with data-driven trigger, migration, restart, canceled intro and reload-at-checkpoint cases.
  - `tests/introPendingPlot.test.ts`: replace its 75-tick trigger; retain pending plot continuation through a saved introductory visit.
  - `tests/demotionNotice.test.ts`: retain machine/notice/render tests; replace all source-regex assertions with recap controller and acknowledgment behavior.
- Extend `tests/campaignSave.test.ts` and `tests/campaignSaveMigration.test.ts` for the new version and trigger fields. Keep `tests/castRegistry.test.ts` locks passing.
- All new tests call public functions, actors or rendered components. No source/CSS regex tests or test-only mutation hooks.

## Save impact

- Allocate the next schema version after #7. If that slice lands v8, S5 lands v9; #11, #12 and #15 must then use v10, v11 and v12.
- Add and validate required boolean `firstConversationDone`; elapsed must be finite and ≥0, without equality to a pacing constant.
- At `emperor_intro`, require done=true and no pending season advance. Preserve the checkpoint whitelist and actor/graph consistency checks.
- Validate legacy inputs using their old rules, migrate, then validate the new schema. Ensure every previously supported version remains accepted.
- Keep elapsed time for unfinished visits and initialize their conversation flag to false. Completed `75` visits remain completed.
- Legacy saves with neither marker remain already introduced. Resume saved `emperor_intro` directly; never re-run its eligibility trigger.
- Migrate `public/qa/romance.json` and `public/qa/jealousy.json` through the parser; both currently store done=true and elapsed=75. Update fixture generation for the new schema.
- Migration changes no RNG, relationships, allowance, rank or tribute history. Test round trips before/after Talk and during the introductory checkpoint.
- Watch index, temporary intents, Bow timers and extras remain presentation data. Defer saved `spotId` to #15.

## Review notes to handle

- Must fix 2: S5 owns the trigger event/data, schema bump, migration and validator change together; coordinate downstream version numbers before implementation.
- Procession frequency: first visit only here. A matching scheduled zone cannot emit a ceremony; future rare events require explicit IDs.
- Placement/opening cast: use actual entry pose, retain independent destination spread, and write beats from the current cast. Never assume Rong or Maid He is active.
- Hook pressure: drive appearance loading, deadline stepping and budget sampling from the existing runtime lifecycle/frame loop; see the owner decisions below.
- Rig corrections: use bone names and procedural gestures. Do not assume a universal joint count, Bow clip or morph targets; emotes remain an optional separate asset.
- Watch-cap balance: preserve #7's present/Talk limits exactly. Verify one shared watch key; carry forward the agreed learner/omniscient simulation gate if pacing changes.
- Witness consistency: retain #4/#7's frozen scene witness list while courtiers move. #11 must preserve preview=receipt when adding geometry.

## Hooks that need the owner's OK

- No new `useEffect`, `useMemo` or `useCallback` is expected. Reuse the palace's existing lifecycle and frame loop; use reducer events and ref callbacks for UI.
- Clock/visibility subscription alternative: feed the clock from existing frame/visibility handlers and existing telemetry callbacks. A new timer or `useSyncExternalStore` subscription needs explicit owner review.
- Emperor load/abort alternative: request/release from appearance state changes inside the runtime. A new effect keyed by watch or procession needs owner OK.
- Transition/Bow timer alternative: injected frame deltas plus CSS animation events. Focus returns through the existing input owner/ref callback; a new focus effect needs owner OK.

## How to check it

1. Start a Concubine run. Observe the actual senior host and companions at Morning Greeting; inspect pond, tea and guqin spots.
2. Walk in through a side gate. Find people near that entrance, then cross the room and verify activities remain spread out.
3. Finish one Talk and leave its scene. Watch the procession; choose Bow once. Repeat on a fresh run without talking and roam for four active minutes.
4. Wait through a watch boundary. Read the new hour under the ink wash; confirm a ready court appears afterward. Open a menu to verify the clock pauses.
5. Play through Rooster in a later season. The Emperor's scheduled location must cause no forced procession. Load an old completed-visit fixture and verify no repeat intro.
6. Try touch, muted sound and reduced motion. Under a throttled device, confirm extras disappear while named courtiers remain available.
7. Load a saved demotion recap. Wait and cross no acknowledgment automatically; Continue acknowledges only the visible recap.

## Done when

- `npm run check` and `npm run build` pass.
- You loaded the game and looked at the change, including phone layout, reduced motion and a watch rebuild.
- Migration fixtures and budget/transition diagnostics demonstrate the criteria above.
- Code review done with GPT-6.1 Sol via T3 `delegate_task` (owner's rule).

title: S4: Replace the header with the Palace HUD, Menu and tracked Map
body:
> Part of #2 · Slice S4 · Size L · Depends on: #4, #6, #7, #8

## What changes for the player

- A round minimap, decree tracker, watch dial, purse and rank seal frame the palace.
- Nearby actions form a short stack. Speak, Enter and Retire share one selected action.
- Esc opens the Palace Menu. People includes Brush Notes; Chronicle holds your notices.
- Map shows this watch's residents. Track points toward a courtier or the gate to their compound.
- Retire at the Ladies' Court bed, or choose “Let the moon pass” in the menu, to end the season early.
- Settings offers Scholar's View and Minimal HUD, with usable layouts on touch screens.

## Why

- The header splits play across Profile, Court, Notifications and Next season (`src/components/GameHeader.tsx:25`).
- The floor plan already updates through telemetry. Adding another minimap would leave two maps (`src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:436`, `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:465`).
- Render code reads actors and panels recompute rules (`src/components/GameLayout.tsx:376`, `src/components/CourtRoster.tsx:27`, `src/components/FactionPanel.tsx:13`).
- Promotion needs both global support and influence. Three faction backers earn an invitation (`src/lib/campaignBalance.ts:68`, `src/lib/factionSystem.ts:199`). The HUD must explain those separately.

## Scope

1. **Finish the shared court view before wiring the HUD.**
   - Extend the minimal `selectCourtView` delivered by #4. Keep its scene callers on the same interface.
   - Derive career/rank labels, taels, global support, influence, promotion targets, deadline, probation, consolidation, audience deferral, access, residents, relationship bands, Brush Notes, plots, reports, notices and available commands.
   - Normalize the legacy scholar role at this boundary. Use `resolveCareer`; keep stored identities unchanged (`src/lib/careerAccess.ts:15`).
   - Build typed `CampaignCommands` once per campaign actor in `main.tsx`. Methods cover existing social/world acts, faction joins, notice acknowledgement and early season advance.
   - Replace `machineState: any` / `send: any` props (`src/components/GameLayout.tsx:104`). HUD and menu bodies consume view data and commands. Actor snapshot access belongs at the boundary.
   - Use the canonical court graph and committed campaign data. If a remaining actor-only field needs a child snapshot, read it in the boundary and prove its updates reach the view.

2. **Make objectives speak the actual rules.**
   - `currentObjectives(view)` returns one to three stable entries. Priority: imminent plot danger, the career decree, then an invitation or useful tip.
   - Absorb the goal selection in `CourtBriefing` (`src/components/CourtBriefing.tsx:14`). Cover promotion, probation, consolidation, missing faction and deferred/final audience.
   - Promotion copy: “Earn the court's regard: 34 of 80 global support · influence 24% of 30% · 11 seasons left.” Derive every target and deadline from the existing rules.
   - With Scholar's View off, influence may use a truthful below/met-target phrase. Decrees always exposes both exact requirements; it never substitutes “3 backers” for global support.
   - Keep faction progress explicitly labelled as invitation progress. Count each courtier against their own backing threshold, with pledges counting; Independent offers no ending.
   - Plot entries name the attacker, target, due season and available defense. Preserve protective casualties and the distinction between player and courtier targets.
   - One tracked line plus up to two muted lines. Do not introduce favour pins, an errand board or invented tasks. Later #12 can supply accepted-favour entries.

3. **Build one palace HUD using the theme.**
   - Add `.hud-root` over the canvas: minimap/tracker top-left; watch dial, purse and Menu/Map/Satchel/People seals top-right; rank bottom-left; interaction stack right-centre.
   - At 1440×900: 24px safe-area gutters, 320px column, 168px round minimap, 46px action rows. Empty HUD space passes pointers to the canvas; controls own their pointers.
   - Use lacquer frames, cinnabar seals, silk menu surfaces, existing fonts, `Emblem` and `PopNumber`. Body text stays at least 13px. Add only missing glyphs needed here: map-pin, archway, bed and action/menu symbols.
   - Add layout/z-order tokens: HUD 20, scene 40, menu 60, ceremony 80. Import unlayered `src/ui/theme/hud.css` after skin through `src/ui/styles.css` (`src/ui/styles.css:20`). No hardcoded UI colors.
   - Show four watch notches: Dragon / Morning Greeting, Horse / Free Hours, Rooster / Dusk Gossip, Rat / Night. Derive the index from the same quarter-season progress used by presence (`src/palace/zones.ts:39`).
   - Read the existing presentation clock. This slice adds no second timer, watch transition, procession or Emperor retime; those belong to #10 and #13.
   - Reuse #6's ToastStack: max four desktop notices, one on touch; queue during dialogue and flush on exit. Plot danger stays assertive. Ordinary notices stay polite.
   - Minimal HUD hides map and tracker. Keep menu access, action prompts and danger notifications usable; expose ongoing plot/report danger on the menu seal and in Decrees.
   - At ≤780px or coarse pointer: 112px minimap, one tracker line, compact dial/purse, 52px stack rows above the touch action cluster and safe-area insets. Keep landscape usable.
   - Move controls help to Settings. A first-run chip may dismiss through CSS animation completion; reduced motion must still reach a dismissed state.

4. **Replace nearest-target selection with a shared interaction stack.**
   - `rankInteractables(pose, entities)` returns at most four candidates with stable id, verb, label, distance, enabled flag and disabled reason.
   - Supply reachable courtier, gate, steward and bed entities. The steward uses #7's buy flow. Listen/Gather/Bow appear only when a later slice supplies a real action.
   - Preserve grounded, readiness, distance, access and clear-path checks. Gate reach is currently 2.8m (`src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:209`); courtier reach is 2.7m (`src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:392`).
   - Rank reachable enabled candidates before locked ones, then distance, then stable id. Preserve the selected id while it remains present; otherwise select the first candidate. Show access reasons on locked rows.
   - E, clicking a row and touch Interact execute the same highlighted candidate. Revalidate it at execution; stale positions or rank changes cannot bypass a gate.
   - Wheel/Up/Down choose rows while the stack is hovered/focused. Consume those events there; elsewhere wheel retains camera zoom and arrows retain movement.
   - Route the existing playtest Interact command through this selection too. Preserve touch joystick, sprint and jump behavior.
   - Register Retire at the existing bed (-14,-25), with an approach point outside its collider on the south side (`src/palace/world.ts:211`). Confirm before advancing.
   - All careers retain the menu alternative; access to the Ladies' Court bed is never required to advance.

5. **Replace the floor plan with the minimap and tracked Map.**
   - Round minimap: camera-yaw rotation, north mark, zone bounds, faint collider footprints, accessible/locked archways, player arrow, visible courtier portrait seals, relationship bands, hostile edges and steward marker.
   - Render report/suspicion eye pips without revealing hidden traits or factions. Reuse the discovery policy already established by #4–#8.
   - Drive `MinimapHandle.update(telemetry)` from the existing ~10Hz frame-loop bridge. Update moving marks imperatively; React receives changed candidates and campaign/watch data rather than every frame.
   - Full Map: five compound tiles around a corridor node, with Emperor north, Library northwest, Dowager west, Empress east and Ladies south. Every compound has gates to every other (`src/palace/zones.ts:26`).
   - Desktop layout is 64% ink plan / 36% resident list and detail; stack these on narrow screens. Accessible labels and the list provide the same information as the SVG.
   - List only this season's living, unexpelled residents. Use `scheduledNpcZone` and career access; locked compounds show hatching and the actual required rank, without revealing their residents.
   - Track stores `{courtierId}` in UI state. Same-zone targets get a gold diamond, clamped at the rim; other-zone targets point to the matching current-zone gate.
   - Resolve the destination again when watch, zone or rank changes. Track never teleports or opens a conversation. Clear it on removal/death; show an access reason and suspend guidance if the new destination becomes locked.
   - Future ear/gather/favour marks are supplied by #11/#12. Do not fabricate them or add campaign fields for them here.

6. **Unroll the Palace Menu and give keyboard input one owner.**
   - A focus-contained silk scroll over the still-rendering, blurred world, capped at 1200×760 and 92vw×86vh. Opening it locks world input and pauses the campaign clock through #4's `worldMode`.
   - Left column: portrait, career/rank, season, global support and influence threads. “Let the moon pass” is its single primary action; it opens a confirmation with plot/deadline warnings.
   - Bed and menu confirmation call the same `advanceSeason` command, routed through existing `NEXT_SEASON` (`src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:763`). Pending/blocked transitions disable it; repeated activation advances once.
   - A paused menu must still permit confirmed early advance. Do not guard the command with `clockRunning`; guard it with campaign eligibility and pending state.
   - Eight tabs: Decrees; People with Brush Notes; Satchel items/detail; Map; Factions with existing intrigue content; Chronicle; Settings; Save.
   - Reuse roster/faction/intrigue bodies after converting actor props to `CourtView` data. Preserve invitations, exact danger thresholds, casualties and useful guide content.
   - Chronicle replaces #6's temporary notices screen, using its bounded log and `ACK_NOTICES`. Opening it cannot repay gifts, reroll results or advance the season. Keep its unread count on the menu entry.
   - Settings: 5/10/15/20-minute seasons, sound, Scholar's View, Minimal HUD and controls/guide. Keep whisper hint controls unavailable until #11 supplies whispers. Keep Scholar's View on until #3's learner gate and owner decision permit hiding numbers.
   - Save embeds the existing storage/recovery body. Preserve backup confirmation and save warnings; keep the pre-campaign/game-over save entry where needed (`src/main.tsx:85`, `src/main.tsx:115`).
   - Persist display preferences through one `src/ui` prefs module with storage-failure defaults. Waypoint, menu tab and selected action remain local UI state.
   - Route `onHotkey` before the movement early-return in the existing listener (`src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:249`). No second global hotkey listener.
   - Roam: Esc Menu, M Map tab, B Satchel tab, C People tab, E highlighted action. Preserve WASD, Shift, Space and R. Scene tools use T Auto, L Log, H Hide, V Dossier; replace A/D labels and bindings from #4.
   - Esc precedence: cancel top confirmation/detail drawer; otherwise dismiss an allowed ceremony/mandatory overlay according to its existing contract; otherwise close Palace Menu; otherwise close the dialogue's local tool/strip; otherwise leave dialogue; otherwise open Menu in roam.
   - Mandatory encounters with no dismiss action consume Esc. A single press never both leaves a scene and opens Menu. Menu shortcuts are inactive during mandatory scenes/transitions.
   - Left/Right switch tabs only when the tab rail owns focus. Form inputs/contenteditable retain typing and native keys; ignore modifiers, repeat toggles and already-consumed events.
   - Reset held keyboard/touch movement when input locks. Restore focus to the connected trigger on exit, or the canvas if that trigger disappeared.
   - Remove deleted panel flags from `worldMode` only after their replacement is wired. Keep demotion, promotion, save confirmation, transition, readiness and hidden-tab blocking covered.

## Delete in the same PR

- `GameHeader` and its header brand/resources/action row; `CourtBriefing` once objectives owns its behavior; the separate Stats/Profile modal after moving useful content into Menu.
- The whole `.palace-map` tree, `mapPlayer` ref (`src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:105`), its telemetry writes, `.map-plan`, `.map-player`, `.map-north` and every responsive override. Keep `zoneGates`, which navigation still needs.
- Legacy nearest-only HUD state/rendering, `.palace-interaction`, `.palace-help`, `.palace-location`, bottom controls strip, old clock and report/plot banners after their replacements work.
- Separate roster/factions/notifications dialog wrappers and #6's stopgap notices list. Retain the reusable bodies; remove their nested dialog launchers.
- Roam Save & game launcher and 2D toggle. Respect the resolved 2D decision from #5; this slice does not silently delete a retained accessibility route.
- Obsolete selectors in `src/style.css`, `src/palace/{palace,touch-controls,zones}.css`, campaign-save CSS and skin. Delete moved rules; retain unrelated world, touch and ceremony styling.
- Update `AGENTS.md` with `src/hud/` ownership and the unlayered `hud.css` exception. Update the architecture map, retire roadmap #4 and document the objective/tracking interfaces and watch vocabulary.

## New or changed modules

| Module | Public interface | What it hides |
|---|---|---|
| `src/lib/courtView.ts` | `selectCourtView(snapshot, ui): CourtView`; typed `CampaignCommands` | Actor/graph projection, rule derivation, role normalization and event payloads. Extend #4's interface. |
| `src/lib/objectives.ts` | `currentObjectives(view): Objective[]` | Career goal selection, danger priority and truthful progress copy. |
| `src/palace/interactables.ts` | `rankInteractables(pose, entities): Candidate[]` | Shared reachability/order/lock reasons; renderer supplies positions and clear-path results. |
| `src/hud/` | `PalaceHud`, `PalaceMenu`, `PalaceMap`; `MinimapHandle.update(telemetry)` | Minimap, DecreeTracker, WatchDial, InteractionStack, tab/focus/confirmation flow and waypoint-to-gate guidance. |
| `src/ui/` | Preference read/write functions; shared Emblem exports | Local display settings, defaults and safe persistence. |
| Existing menu bodies | `CourtView` slices plus commands | Reuse roster, factions, intrigue and save behavior without actor reads or duplicate dialogs. |

Keep rules pure and deterministic. No new gameplay states, random draws, save fields or single-implementation ports. Each module starts with an ownership comment.

## Tests

- Add `courtView` interface fixtures for all careers/ranks, actor-only updates, graph projections, access, notices, plots and removed residents. Assert selection never sends events or mutates input.
- Add objectives tables for each promotion boundary: one bar met, both met, probation, rank deadlines, top consolidation, audience deferral and faction invitation. Three backers alone must not imply promotion.
- Add interaction tables for ties, ≤4 cap, locked gates, clear-path rejection, airborne/not-ready state, stable selection and bed approach outside the collider.
- Render HUD/Menu/Map fixtures: eight tabs, two promotion requirements, locked hatch, eligible presence seals, unknown knowledge, Chronicle unread state, danger copy and minimal/touch variants.
- Test waypoint guidance through its public interface: same-zone mark, cross-zone gate, watch relocation, locked destination, target death/removal and clearing.
- Exercise hotkey/menu handlers in a DOM/browser test: Esc precedence, native cancel, focus return, typed input, no WASD collisions, selection keys and touch action parity. Verify menus pause clock/input while rendering continues.
- Actor-backed early-advance test: cancel sends nothing; confirm from bed or paused menu advances once; a pending/mandatory scene cannot advance. Chronicle acknowledgement changes only read state.
- Replace every affected existing test below; retain unrelated machine/save assertions. Check the inherited branch for replacements already landed by dependencies.

| Existing file affected | Interface-level replacement |
|---|---|
| `tests/rankGiftIncome.test.ts` | Replace GameHeader/Profile render case with PalaceMenu career summary and accessible menu controls. Keep all allowance/reload cases. |
| `tests/courtIntrigueUI.test.ts` | Replace banner/source and CSS-regex cases with Scheme tracker, assertive toast and Factions tab render/behavior tests. Preserve exact due season, defense threshold and casualty checks. |
| `tests/uiKit.test.ts` | Adapt FactionPanel fixture to view data; retain faction glyph/label checks and other UI tests. |
| `tests/campaignRoleSelection.test.ts` | Render the embedded Save body for each career; retain choose-path, backup and recovery tests. |
| `tests/giftNotifications.test.ts` / #6's replacement | Replace remaining header/stopgap-list renders with Chronicle and unread Menu entry tests. Retain bounded log and ack/save idempotency. |
| `tests/romanceUI.test.ts` | Adapt any surviving intrigue-body render to view fixtures; preserve romantic target/protective casualty wording. #4 owns obsolete speech/action-source replacements. |
| `tests/demotionNotice.test.ts` | Preserve recap behavior; if the layout refactor breaks source assertions, replace those with overlay/command tests proving deadline ACK and audience ACK cannot cross-fire. Keep saved notice tests. |

No tests that read source or CSS text. `tests/emperorIntro.test.ts`, zone/access, schedule and asset lifecycle behavior must remain green; do not rewrite their gameplay contracts.

## Save impact

- No campaign schema bump. Reuse the save/notice/item fields landed by #6/#7.
- Menu tab, selected row, waypoint and confirmations never enter the save. Preferences are separate local settings. Loading a campaign clears stale tracking and confirmations.
- Reuse the existing presentation clock/pose and persistence lifecycle; menu pause and acknowledgement cannot reset remaining time, awards, support or RNG.

## Review notes to handle

- Must fix #12: use global support plus influence targets and the real deadline; backers appear only in invitation copy. Add separate promotion/invitation boundary fixtures.
- Must fix #9: converge on #4's `worldMode`; remove the old panel pause flags only with their wrappers, and test every surviving overlay and input path.
- Should fix “Two minimaps” / “notices log”: remove the whole old floor plan; replace #6's stopgap with Chronicle without losing read state or notices.
- Should fix “CourtView comes too late”: extend the view first introduced in #4. No new ad-hoc actor reads in HUD/menu bodies.
- Should fix “still reads like a form”: the tracker shows real career/danger context and at most three lines. Accepted favours remain a later optional feature; no pin-filled quest board or arbitrary satchel capacity display.
- Should fix “Hotkeys collide” / “Hook pressure”: apply the concrete bindings/Esc order above; route focus and telemetry through existing edges. List proposed hook changes below before implementation.
- Should fix “AGENTS.md updates” / “Owner process”: document HUD/CSS ownership and complete GPT review through T3. Hidden numbers need the learner gate and the owner's decision; default Scholar's View stays on.

## Hooks that need the owner's OK

- New `useEffect`, `useMemo`, `useCallback` or additional subscriptions require the owner's OK for this slice; none is necessary for layout/objective derivation.
- Menu focus/showModal: reuse the existing `CourtDialog` lifecycle (`src/components/CourtDialog.tsx:7`) or use a ref callback plus native focus/cancel handling. An extra effect would need OK.
- Live child actor data: prefer existing `useMachine`/selector subscriptions and canonical graph projection. Any extra actor subscription must be listed with cleanup and approved; alternative is passing already-subscribed snapshots into the selector.
- Minimap telemetry, hotkeys, visibility and candidate refresh: reuse the existing frame loop/listeners and refs. No per-frame React subscription or new keyboard/visibility effect.
- Preferences and first-run chip: state/reducer initialization, explicit event writes and `onAnimationEnd`. No synchronization/timer effects. No memo/callback hooks merely for performance without evidence.

## How to check it

1. Start each career. Walk with WASD; inspect the round map, truthful decree, watch dial, taels and rank seal. Approach a courtier and gate; change the highlighted action and use E.
2. Press Esc. Visit all eight tabs. Compare Decrees against standing/influence targets; inspect People/Brush Notes, faction invitations, Chronicle and Save recovery options.
3. Press M in roam. Track an accessible courtier in another compound; follow the gate arrow. Let a watch change and confirm guidance follows their new destination. Locked compounds explain the required rank.
4. Open Menu for several seconds; confirm the clock and movement stop. Press Esc once to close it. Open dialogue, its Dossier and a confirmation; each Esc closes only the top allowed layer.
5. At the Ladies' Court bed, choose Retire and cancel. Confirm again: one season advances. Repeat through “Let the moon pass” as Prince or Scholar.
6. Inspect a plot warning, then enable Minimal HUD. Danger remains discoverable and announced; Chronicle opens without changing taels or season. Scholar's View reveals exact requirements.
7. Check 390×844 and phone landscape: stack clears joystick/actions, rows remain tappable, tabs and Map scroll. Repeat with reduced motion and the software renderer.

## Done when

- `npm run check` and `npm run build` pass.
- You loaded the game and looked at the change on desktop and touch layouts.
- The old floor plan, header and stopgap notices screen have been removed; one input path and one minimap remain.
- Promotion copy, Chronicle acknowledgement, tracking, pause and early-advance tests pass.
- Code review done with GPT-6.1 Sol via T3 `delegate_task` (owner's rule).

title: S3: Voices of the Ladies' Court
body:
> Part of #2 · Slice S3 · Size L · Depends on: #4, #7

## What changes for the player

- Ten courtiers have distinct greetings, reactions and written replies.
- Greetings reflect your bond and rank. Rong is acid; Zhen is prim; Maid He is chatty.
- Nearby name plaques open into short barks, with at most two visible at once.
- Taste hints add suspected facts to Brush Notes. A hint keeps its speaker and source.
- Reloading preserves the last committed response. Repainting the scene cannot reroll it.

## Why

- Everyone currently shares six response banks, drawn with `Math.random` (`src/lib/getResponse.ts:2`, `src/lib/getResponse.ts:37`).
- One gift draws separately for the courtier and campaign response (`src/state-machines/character-machine.ts:82`, `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:513`). The texts can disagree.
- Speaker prefixes are stripped or rewritten in three UI paths (`src/components/CourtSpeechBubble.tsx:2`, `src/components/GameLayout.tsx:157`, `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:398`).
- Consorts and concubines total ten already, while maids rotate through three zones (`src/lib/courtHierarchy.ts:6`, `src/lib/courtHierarchy.ts:10`, `src/palace/zones.ts:53`). The authored cohort must be explicit.

## Scope

1. **Freeze the authored cohort and write the style bible.**
   - These are the ten personal voices for this slice; residence remains governed by the existing schedule.
   - Consort Rong: acid courtesy, compliments with a barb.
   - Consort Zhen: precise etiquette, protective reprimands.
   - Consort Hua: diplomatic warmth, tactful redirection.
   - Consort Yue: composed musical imagery, measured pauses.
   - Concubine Mei: observant warmth, small social gambits.
   - Concubine Lin: clipped wit, careful deflection.
   - Concubine Xia: direct curiosity, quick challenges.
   - Concubine Yun: restrained imagery, quiet doubts.
   - Concubine An: calm musical detail, understated humour.
   - Maid He: practical tea-room gossip, chatty taste hints.
   - These are writing directions. They do not change personality vectors, factions or gift rules.
   - Existing identities: `src/data/characters.ts:123`, `src/data/courtExpansion.ts:14`, `src/data/courtExpansion.ts:109`, `src/data/courtExpansion.ts:173`.
   - Concubine Qiao and the other 37 courtiers use fallback packs until #16. Do not rename or add actors.
   - `docs/court-voice.md`: register, rank-specific address, contractions, humour, individual motifs and example exchanges.
   - Use “this servant” and “this palace” where rank and situation justify them. Keep the dry humour of `DEATH_METHODS` (`src/lib/courtPlots.ts:10`).
   - Avoid modern customer-service phrasing, exposition dumps and identical stock courtesies.

2. **Extract the cosmetic draw without changing plot outcomes.**
   - Add `cosmeticPick<T>(seed, key, options)` using the existing FNV calculation (`src/lib/courtPlots.ts:19`).
   - Reject empty options explicitly. Keep unsigned seed handling and array order deterministic.
   - Make `deathMethodFor` delegate with its existing seed and `${season}:${attacker}:${victim}` key. Preserve exact picks.
   - Voice draws use the stable `campaignSeed` supplied by #7, never the changing `rngState`.
   - Keys include name, slot, season, watch, situation and stable turn/request identity.
   - Re-renders, frame counts, wall time and `Math.random` must never select a line.

3. **Build courtVoice and author its content.**
   - Resolve a personal override, then an office/temperament pack, then a safe generic line.
   - Accept typed scene data from the minimal `selectCourtView` delivered in #4. Do not read actors inside voice code.
   - Reuse office, career, bond-band and verdict types from their owning modules.
   - Declare roughly 15 slots: greeting, farewell, five present verdicts, four talk reactions, activity, taste hint, gossip and witnessed reaction.
   - Define the mapping from #7 talk outcomes to reaction slots once; keep every gameplay result unchanged.
   - Cover Stranger, Acquainted, Trusted, Confidante and Sworn; rank changes address and etiquette.
   - Initial budget: about 450 shared pack lines, 350 personal lines, 120 player replies and 40 taste-hint variants: about 960 authored strings.
   - Shared lines may cover compatible bands. Count distinct authored strings separately from resolved coverage cells.
   - Every authored courtier needs personal greetings across all five bands, personal present reactions, contextual replies and personal barks.
   - Validate supported office/temperament combinations for these ten, including alternate seeded personalities.
   - Plan content review in two batches: shared packs/style bible, then ten personal banks and replies. Expand the budget if coverage exposes holes.
   - #16 owns the remaining personal banks and full-court completeness. The overall project needs 3,000+ strings across all content systems.

4. **Replace response generation at the committed-event boundary.**
   - Current calls are `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:513`, `src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:647` and `src/state-machines/character-machine.ts:82`.
   - #7 replaces their gift protocol. Integrate with its `applySocialAct` and `APPLY_SOCIAL_RESULT` path; do not restore the removed pipeline.
   - Pick each committed reaction once. Carry the exact text through the receipt, actor event and campaign response.
   - Store plain line text in existing response strings. Keep speaker identity separate in the scene view.
   - Duplicate request IDs must retain the original receipt and response, with no additional knowledge or awards.
   - Pure scene greetings are picked once on scene entry and retained through its beat flow.
   - Put contextual player replies in the content banks and expose them through `courtTalk.talkOptions` and `conversationChoices`.
   - Author two to four situation-specific choices with stable IDs and hidden scoring metadata; preserve #7 gating and effects.
   - Never render a fixed loyal/ambitious/neutral trio or recycle the same three sentences for each courtier.
   - Example: Rong discussing a poor present might offer “Ask what would better suit her table” or “Make a dry joke about its journey.” Other situations need their own wording.
   - Display names come from CourtView. Any old prefixed saved text is normalized once at the existing restore/view boundary.

5. **Add barks to the existing projected labels.**
   - Labels are created at `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:189` and projected at `src/palace/PalaceScene.tsx:394`.
   - Extend each label with separate name and bark nodes. Stop whole-label `textContent` updates from erasing the bark.
   - In roam mode, select at most two ready, visible, unobstructed courtiers within 10 m; rank by distance and stable name tie-break.
   - Trigger on approach or a new eligible situation. Hold a bark for about four seconds and use a per-courtier/watch cooldown.
   - Keep scheduling in the existing frame loop, using elapsed frame time. Never choose again on every frame.
   - Hide barks during dialogue, menus and cutscenes using #4 worldMode. Keep timing frozen when the world is frozen.
   - Expand the name into a chamfered lacquer plaque with theme tokens, body text at least 13 px and restrained motion.
   - Keep name and line legible on phones. Respect reduced motion. Add no emoji or plain rounded cards.
   - Add styles to the theme; remove only the legacy label rules this change supersedes. Leave unrelated HUD work to #9.
   - Provide one polite accessible announcement per newly shown bark; decorative projected duplicates are aria-hidden.
   - Taste hints carry typed facts from the existing tastes catalogue, with courtier, source and suspected certainty.
   - Record a hint only when shown, through a validated, deduplicated campaign command using #7 Brush Notes. Rendering alone must not write campaign state.
   - Never record a suspected hint as a confirmed gift verdict. Choosing or suppressing a bark consumes no gameplay RNG.
   - Gossip uses supplied real graph/plot facts; witnessed reactions use accepted action data. Missing facts suppress that slot.
   - #11 owns spatial overhearing and rumour mechanics. This slice must not invent secrets, reports or witness geometry.

## Delete in the same PR

- Delete `src/lib/getResponse.ts`, its imports and the `GiftResponse` type derived from its function signature (`src/state-machines/game-machine.ts:117`).
- Remove separate parent/actor response draws and superseded generic reply tables.
- Remove any surviving speaker-prefix parsing from the three UI paths above; #4 may already have removed them.
- Remove the inline FNV implementation from `deathMethodFor`, while retaining its public domain function and death-method catalogue.
- Delete only superseded label CSS from legacy files. Add no new rules to legacy CSS.

## New or changed modules

- `src/lib/cosmeticDraw.ts`: `cosmeticPick(seed, key, options)` hides stable indexing; plots and voice share it.
- `src/lib/courtVoice.ts`: `speak(name, slot, context) → {speaker, line, hint?}` hides voice resolution, contextual selection and safe fallbacks.
- Its context includes bond, career, temperament, stable seed/turn keys and typed situation facts. Optional hints are data, never side effects.
- `src/data/court/voicePacks.ts` and `src/data/court/heroes/*.ts`: authored content behind courtVoice; callers never traverse pack tables.
- Existing courtTalk/conversation modules: contextual reply IDs/text and hidden scoring metadata through their existing interfaces.
- Existing machine/router and CourtView: one committed line and one typed knowledge command; preserve #7 serial and idempotency rules.
- PalaceScene: projected bark nodes and lifecycle in the existing frame loop. Keep voice selection out of React render.
- `docs/court-voice.md` plus the module map: register, cohort, content budget and ownership.

## Tests

- Add cosmeticDraw interface tests: deterministic picks, empty-bank error, varied keys and a throwing `Math.random` stub.
- Keep `tests/courtPlots.test.ts`; add exact pre-extraction death-method examples and unchanged gameplay RNG results.
- Add courtVoice completeness over exactly these ten × supported slots × five bands × applicable rank/situation variants.
- Assert non-empty lines, at most 140 characters per NPC line, no emoji, correct speaker and required personal overrides. Count unique strings in the budget receipt.
- Test personal/office/generic resolution through `speak`; safe fallbacks for the other 38 get smoke coverage only.
- Render contextual reply choices for Rong, Zhen and Maid He; inspect text and stable IDs, including changed situations. No source or CSS regex tests.
- Extend the #4 DialogueScene tests: full accessible subtitle, correct display name, exact committed line and no repeated bark announcements on repaint.
- Extend #7 social transaction/machine tests: displayed reaction = receipt = actor `lastResponse` = campaign response; retry leaves each unchanged.
- Extend `tests/campaignSave.test.ts` and `tests/romanceLifecycle.test.ts`: committed text survives reload; old prefixed text displays correctly once normalized.
- Test bark scheduling through its runtime interface with fake elapsed time and candidate positions: two-line cap, 10 m radius, occlusion, cooldown, frozen/hidden modes and cleanup.
- Test suspected hint deduplication through the campaign interface; hidden/suppressed barks add no facts and no RNG draws.
- No current suite directly imports getResponse. `tests/romanceUI.test.ts` assertions against deleted speech components must already be replaced by #3/#4; port any survivors to DialogueScene interface tests.
- #7 owns replacement of `tests/giftTransactions.test.ts` and its removed async protocol. Extend that replacement rather than keeping legacy events for this slice.
- Keep cast/asset and schedule tests unchanged. This slice changes no models, residence rules or active-cast selection.

## Save impact

- No additional schema bump beyond #7 v8. Use its `campaignSeed` and Brush Notes fields.
- Existing response fields remain strings; current validators accept them (`src/persistence/campaignSave.ts:83`, `src/persistence/campaignSave.ts:144`).
- Bark timers, visible lines and scene turns are transient. Derive stable draw keys from existing campaign/scene identities.
- Restore must keep committed text rather than regenerating it from a potentially revised content bank.

## Review notes to handle

- Red-team Must fix 1: stable cosmetic seed comes from #7; never derive voice seed from the live RNG stream.
- Undefined “Ladies' Court 10”: the exact cohort above includes Maid He. It changes neither the 48-name roster nor scheduled presence.
- Content undercount: budget player replies and hints explicitly; scope exhaustive voice coverage to ten, with full-court coverage deferred to #16.
- Tone-picker concern: author contextual replies with hidden metadata; no fixed stance labels in the player UI.
- CourtView timing and actor protocol: use #4 selector and #7 social result contract, including serial handling and duplicate requests.
- Random opening cast: browser QA needs a deterministic fixture containing the named test speakers. Do not guarantee all ten in a normal season.
- Typewriter accessibility: preserve #4 full-line live text and aria-hidden character animation; the bark adds only one announcement.

## Hooks that need the owner's OK

- None expected beyond the existing PalaceScene lifecycle and #4 scene hooks.
- Use its frame loop/live props for bark updates and existing callbacks for knowledge commands. Use a ref callback for the accessible bark node.
